Diodorus be of reputation in Babylon as the priest in Egypt chaldaean be a name sometime apply to the whole nation sometime appropriate to the priest who spend their whole time in religious service and in astrology many of they by divination foretell thing to come as we have show before in the history of Alexander and the book of Daniel witness this their profession by their augury or divination by bird by sacrifice and enchantment they be account to do good or harm to mankind they be most expert in their sacred rite in the knowledge whereof they be bring up from their childhood and continue in that course of learn all their life the child be instruct in his father science they profess the interpretation of dream and prodigious accident in nature their opinion be that the world be eternal without beginning and end the order and furniture of all be do by divine providence all heavenly thing be perfect not by chance of their own accord but by the determinate and firm decree of the god by long observation search the course and nature of the star they foretell thing to come but the great power they attribute to the five planet and especial to Saturn they call they mercuries because when other be fix these have their proper motion and show future thing as the interpreter of the god by their rise set and colour under their course they give the title of god b b to thirty other star the one half above the other under the earth behold all accident and in ten day one of the high be send to the low as a angel or messenger of the star and one from they to the high and this course they take eternal they hold twelve principal god each of which have his peculiar month and his sign in the zodiac by which the sun and moon and five planet have their motion these planet they esteem to confer much good or evil in the generation of man and by their nature and aspect thing to come may be foreknow many thing they foretell to Alexander Nicanor Antigonus Seleucus and to private man of they above four thousand call Essaei (@) (@) (@) (@) (@) that be holy not sacrifice other creature but their mind unto God some of they be husbandman some artificer for necessity not for abundance they make no weapon of war nor meddle with merchandise they have no servant but be all both free and mutual servant to each other they live perpetual chaste swear not at all nor lie esteem God the giver of all good and author of no evil their society be such that one garment one house one food one treasury one get one spend one life be in common to they all careful provide for their sick and hold the elder man in place of parent josephus who himself live among they do more large describe they h h joseph de bel. jud. lib. 2. cap. 7. he report that they be by nation Jew avoid pleasure and riches as sin account continence and contentedness great virtue they marry not but instruct the child of other respect they as their kindred in their manner not deny the lawfulness of marriage but the honesty of woman he which become one of their fraternity must make his good common oil and neatness they shun yet wear always a white garment they have officer for their common provision they have no one certain city but in each many of they have their house to stranger of their own sect they communicate their good and acquaintance and therefore carry nothing with they in their journey but weapon for fear of thief and in every city have of the same college a especial officer which provide for stranger the child under tuition of master be alike provide for nor do they change their raiment till the old be wear they neither buy nor sell but mutual communicate devout they be in the service of God for before the sun rise they speak of no profane or worldly matter but celebrate certain prayer as i i the essee be worshipper of the sun hence come the (@) (@) (@) (@) (@) and sampsaei pray he to rise then by their officer be each appoint to their work till the five hour at which time they assemble together and be gird with linen garment wash themselves with cold water then do they go into their dining-room as into a temple where no man of another sect may be admit and there stay with silence the pantler set they bread in order and the cook one vessel of broth the priest give thanks as after dinner also then lay aside those their holy garment they ply their work till the evening and then sup in like manner there be never cry or tumult they speak in order and observe even without the house a venerable silence in other thing they be subject to their overseer but at their own choice may help and show mercy to other to their kindred they can give without licence what they say be certain but a oath they hate no less than perjury they study the writing of the ancient thence collect such thing as may benefit the manner of the mind or health of the body they which be studious of their sect must a year space endure trial and then after that probation of their continency must be probationer yet two year long and then upon allowance of their manner be assume into their fellowship make first deep protestation of religion towards God and justice towards man to keep faith to all but especial to prince and if they shall come to rule over other not to abuse their power not to exceed other in habit not to steal not to keep any thing secret from they of their own sect or cummunicate it to another although upon peril of life not to devise new doctrine to keep the book of their own opinion and the name of the angel offender they put from their fellowship and he which be Asia now Zuiria lie north and east betwixt Iberia and the sea of which Strabo affirm that they need not the sea who make no better use of the land for they bestow not the least labour in husbandry and yet the earth voluntary and liberal yield her store and where it be once sow it may twice or thrice be reap the man be so simple that they neither have use of money nor do they number above a hundred ignorant of weight measure war civility husbandry there be in use among they six and twenty language they have f f Sansovinus and report of such spider in Italy in Calabria call spider which will procure death upon man smile and some also which do man to die weep they worship the sun jupiter and the moon who temple be near to Iberia the priest which rule it be next in honour to the king he perform the holy rite rule the holy region which be large and full of people of the sacred servant many be inspire do divine or prophecy he which be most ravish with the spirit wander alone through the wood he the priest take and bind with a sacred chain allow he sumptuous nourishment the space of a year and after bring he to be slay with other sacrifice to the goddess the rite be thus one which be skilful of this business hold the sacred spear wherewith they use to slay the man step forth thrust it into his heart in his fall they observe certain token of divination then do they bring out the body into some place where they all go over it the albanian honour old-age in all man death in none account it unlawful to mention a dead man with who they also bury his wealth g g plin. lib. 7. their manner and custom he thus report they have no limitation of land nor tillage nor house but always wander through place not inhabit feed their herd and flock they carry their wife and child with they on cart which also be cover with hide they use for house no offence be more heinous among they then theft gold and silver they as much contemn as other desire milk and honey be their food their they worship first Vesta who they call in their language Tabiti next of all jupiter in their speech papaeus and the earth suppose she to be the wife of jupiter and call she apia in the next place they worship Apollo and Venus by the name of Octosyrus and Artimpasa and Mars and Hercules some of they sacrifice also to Neptune or Thamimasades image altar and temple they think ought not to be make except to Mars their manner of sacrifice be general this the sacrifice be present with the forefoot bind the sacrificer at his back have lay aside his holy vestment wound the same and while it fall call upon that god to who he sacrifice and then put a halter about the neck and strangle it without kindle any fire or vow or other ceremony and slay it the flesh pluck from the bone he cast into a great cauldron the bone he use for fuel to seethe the same for wood the country do not yield and if they have not any such vessel they put all the flesh with water into the paunch and so the beast do seethe itself after it be boil he which sacrifice offer the libament or offering of the flesh and innards their sacrifice be beside other beast especial of horse their temple to Mars they build on this manner scythian temple they heap together bundle of twig three furlong in length and breadth and above on they be make a square plain three side thereof be upright the four be make slope and the bending-wise thereby to get up thither they bring every year a hundred and fifty wane of twig to supply the waste of they underneath this work be erect a old iron sword and this be their image of Mars to which they offer yearly sacrifice both of other cattle and of horse and more to this blade then to other god of their captive they offer one of a hundred but after another manner for after they have offer wine on their head they kill they by a certain vessel and after lift they upon that their heap or temple they imbrue the sword-god with the blood this they do above beneath in the temple they cut off all the right shoulder of the slay man and hurl they up in the air together with the hand wheresoever the hand shall fall there it lie and the dead body apart when they have perform all their solemnity they depart swine be so odious to they that they will have none of they nourish in their country there be among they diviner who rite be these scythian divination they bring great bundle of willow twig which they lie on the ground and untie and lay they asunder one by one divine some of they practice divination with the leaf of the teil-tree which they fold and unfold in their hand the king when at any time he fall sick send for three choice man of those diviner who for the most part name some man unto he which have forswear himself have swear by the king throne a oath use of the scythian present the man be bring forth who if he deny what their art have accuse he of the king send for twice the number of diviner and if they by new practice of their art find he guilty his head be cut off and the first diviner share his good but if they shall absolve he more diviner be send for and if the most of they do absolve he than those three first be thus do to death they lade a wain with twig and bind the diviner hand and foot and stop their mouth cast they into the wane and set all on fire burn ox wain and man together unless some of the ox by the burn of their harness escape this punishment inflict they on their false prophet they make their league with other nation in this sort they pour wine into a great bowl mix therewith the blood of they which join in league cut some part of the body with a knife or sword and then dip in that bowl or mazer a sword arrow a axe a dart and after curse themselves with many word last of all drink the wine Nicephorus p p nic. take view of our tartarian religion chap. 13 of the religion of the tartar and cathayan JOANNES r r io. de pl. car. c. 3. op. Hak. to 1 de plano carpini thus write of their religion they believe that there be one GOD the maker of all thing visible and invisible the author of good thing and punishment yet do they not worship he with prayer praise or any certain rite they have also idol of felt in the fashion of a man and the same they set on both side of their Tent-door and under they they put a thing of felt fashion like a dug these they account the keeper of their cattle author of their milk and young store other they make of silk and do they much honour some place they in a fair chariot cover before the door of their station and whosoever steal any thing out of that chariot be slay without all pity their captain have one always in the midst of their tent. to these idol they offer the first fruit of their milk and the first morsel of their meat and first draught of their drink at meal and when they kill a beast they offer the heart to their idol leave it before he till the morning and then they take and eat it they make a idol also to their chief emperor and offer thereunto with great solemnity as well other creature as horse which none after dare ride on till death they break not a bone of the beast which they kill for meat but burn they with fire they bend themselves to this idol towards the south as to a God they worship the sun light and fire water also and the earth offer thereunto the first of their meat and drink and in the morning before they eat or drink they have no set rite prescribe by law nor do they compel any to deny their religion simple although in some of their custom they be very rigorous thus they martyr Michael duke of Russia because he refuse to do reverence to the image of Cingis can which have be their first emperor and compel the young brother of Andrew duke of Saruogle in Russia to marry his say brother wife according to their custom after that they have slay her former husband they have certain tradition their sin according to which they reckon these thing follow to be sin to thrust a knife into the fire or any way touch the fire with a knife or with their knife to take flesh out of the cauldron or to hew with a hatchet near to the fire for they think that they shall so cut away the head of the fire they account it sin also to lean on the whip wherewith they beat their horse for they ride not with spur also to touch arrow with a whip to take or kill young bird to strike a horse with the rain of their bridle and to break one bone against another likewise to pour out meat milk or any kind of drink upon the ground or to make water within their tabernacle which whosoever do willing be slay but otherwise he must pay a great sum of money to the enchanter to be purify who cause the tabernacle with all thing therein to pass between two fire beside if any have a morsel give he which he be not able to swallow and for that cause cast it out of his mouth there be a hole make under his tabernacle by which he be draw forth and slay without all compassion likewise whosoever tread upon the threshold of any of the duke tabernacle he be put to death thus be these gnat strain when as hostile invasion murder and such other camel be easy among they swallow they think that after death they shall live in another world and there multiply their cattle eat drink and do other action of life at a new moon or a full moon they begin all new enterprise they call she the great emperor and bow their knee and pray thereto the sun they say be the moon mother because she have thence her light their sorcery they be give to divination augury sooth-saying witchcraft enchantment and when they receive answer from the devil they attribute the same unto God who they call Itoga and the comanian call he Chan that be emperor who they marvellous fear and reverence offer to he many oblation and the first fruit of their meat and drink according to his answer they dispose all thing they believe that all thing be purge by fire therefore when any ambassador prince or other personage whatsoever come unto they they and their gift must pass between two fire to be purify lest peradventure they have practise some witchcraft or have bring some poison or other mischief with they and if fire fall from heaven upon man or beast which there often happen or if they think themselves any way defile or unclean they thus be purify by their enchanter if any be sick a spear be set up in his tent with black feel welt about it and from thenceforth their sickness and funeral no stranger enter therein for none of they which be present at his death may enter the hoard of any duke or emperor till a new-moon when he be dead if he be a chief man he be bury in the field where please he and he be bury with his tent sit in the midst thereof with a table set before he and a platter full of meat and a cup of Mares-milk there be also bury with he s s vin. l. 30. c. 86. a mare and colt a horse with bridle and saddle and they eat another horse who bone the woman burn for the soul of the dead stuff his hide with straw set it aloft on two or four pole that he may have in the other world a tabernacle and other thing fit for his use they bury his gold and silver with he the chariot or cart in which he be carry forth be break his tent be destroy neither be it lawful to name his name till the three generation they observe also other funeral rite too long to rehearse they lament their dead thirty day more or less their parent and those of their family be thus cleanse they make two fire and pitch near thereunto two spear with a line from the top of the one to the other fasten on the same line some piece of buckram under which and betwixt the fire pass the man beast and tent there stand also two woman one on this side the other on that cast water and repeat certain charm if any thing fall or be break the enchanter have it and if any be slay of thunder the man in the tent must thus be cleanse and all thing in the tent their condition be otherwise repute unclean and not to be touch no man be more obedient to their lord then the tartar they seldom contend in word never in deed they be reasonable courteous one to another their woman be chaste adultery be seldom hear of and theft be rare both punish by death drunkenness common but without brawl among themselves or discredit among other they be proud greedy deceitful they eat dog wolf fox horse and in necessity man flesh mouse and other filth and that in as filthy a manner without clothes and napkin their boot and the grass can serve to wipe their greasy hand they have no beard herb wine meat or beer nor do they wash their dish it be a great sin among they to suffer any of their food to be lose and therefore they will not bestow a bone on a dog till they have eat the marrow side be on the west there be a image with a cow udder for the woman who office it be to milk the kine on the other side another with a mare udder for the men. when they make merry they sprinkle their drink upon these image in order begin at the master then go a servant out of the house with a cup full of drink sprinkle thrice towards the south and bow the knee at every time and this be do for the honour of the fire then perform he the like superstition towards the east for the honour of the air next to the west for the honour of water and last to the north in the behalf of the dead when the master hold a cup in his hand to drink before he taste thereof he pour his part upon the ground if he drink sit on horseback he first pour part thereof on the mane of the horse after the servant aforesaid have discharge his cup to the four quarter of the world he return to the house and two other servant stand ready with two cup and two basin to carry drink unto their master and that wife which lie with he the last night sit together on a bed their soothsayer or enchanter be their priest Rubruq alt. m.s. to this may be add out of the manuscript above mention their divination by three bone through which be first burn black the look and if the sight pass straight and right it be a good token but if it be inward crooked or break he then upon this evil presage cease from his enterprise master jenkinson travel with certain tartar which divine by the blade-bone of sheep sod and then burn to powder which be mingle with the blood of the sheep they write therewith certain character with diverse word and ceremony and thence divine of their success which they find true to their cost they use divination also by four sword mangu can desire a conference betwixt the christian saracen and idolater to see which of they can make best proof of his religion the moal tartar profess to believe one only GOD the author of life and death but as the hand which be one have diverse finger so think he and they that this one GOD be please with diverse way of devotion their priest be diviner they be many but have one captain or chief bishop who always place his house or tent before that of the great can about a stone cast distant he have charge of the wain which carry the idol the other priest have their place appoint they some of they be astrologer special that highpriest which foretell the eclipse of the moon all the people provide they their meat that they may not go out of their tent when a eclipse happen they sound their organ and timbrel and make a great noise and when it be past they make great feast drink and mirth they foretell holiday and those which be unlucky for enterprise no war be begin or make without their word they cause all present which be send to the can to pass through the fire they purify the household of the dead by the like rite which before may not be touch on the nine day of may they assemble all the white mare and hallow they at which the christian must be present with their censor they then cast on the ground new a a churned Mares-milk and make a great feast they foretell the destiny of infant new bear and when one be sick they divine by charm whether the disease be natural or proceed of sorcery they be themselves witch sorcerer inuoker of the devil this they do in the night set flesh in the midst of the house ready boil use charm timbrel and fall into mad fit be bind then come the devil and give they answer thus much rubruquis m. Paulus thus report of their religion they say b b l. 1. c. 46 that there be a GOD on high in heaven of who lift up their hand and smite their tooth three time together every day with censer and incense they desire health and understanding l. 2. c. 26 they place a table aloft in the wall of their house in the which be write a name that represent this god they have another which they call Natigay or Itogay of feel or other stuff in every house they make he a wife and child and set his wife on the left hand and his child before he which seem to do he reverence this they call the god of earthly thing which keep their child beast and corn and when they eat they anoint his mouth with the fat and the mouth of his wife and child and then cast out the broth out of the door unto other spirit and when their God have have his part they take they of this Natigay they with like ceremony of lift up their hand and smite of their tooth desire temperature of the air l. 2. c. 26. fruit of the earth child and such like their wife be exceed chaste and observant and though they be many yet can Rachel and Leah yea ten or twenty of they agree with a marvelous union intent unto their household and other business whereby they be gainful and not chargeable to their husband when they marry n n w. de rich. in this sort the husband covenant with the father of the maid who have give he power to take she wheresoever he shall find she he seek she among some of her friend where she have then of purpose hide herself and by a kind of force carry she away they marry with any except their own mother and sister their widow seldom marry because of their service to their former husband in another world except the son marry his father wife or the brother his brother because they can there in the next world be content to resign they to their former husband again the woman buy sell and provide all necessary into the house the man intend nothing but their arm hunt and hawk if one have bury a male-child and another a female the parent contract a marriage betwixt those two and paint in paper servant horse clothes and household and make writing for the confirmation of the dower burn these thing in the fire by the smoke whereof they in their smoky conceit imagine all these thing to be carry and confirm to their child in the other world and the parent of the two dead party claim kindred each of other as if they indeed have marry their child while they live in Xamdu do Cublai can build a stately palace encompass sixteen mile of plain ground with a wall wherein be fertile meadow pleasant spring delightful stream and all sort of beast of chase and game and in the midst thereof a sumptuous house of pleasure which may be remove from place to place here he do abide in the month of june july and August on the eight and twenty day whereof he depart thence to another place to do sacrifice on this manner he have a herd or drive of horse and mare about ten thousand as white as snow of the milk whereof none may taste except he be of the blood of Cingis can. yea the tartar do these beast great reverence nor dare any cross their way or go before they according to the direction of his astrologer or magician he on the eight and twenty of August aforesaid spend and pour forth with his own hand the milk of these mare in the air and on the earth to give drink to the spirit and idol which they worship that they may preserve the man woman beast bird corn and other thing grow on the earth their sect and order these astrologer or necromancer be in their art marvelous when the sky be cloudy and threaten rain they will ascend the roof of the palace of the grand can and cause the rain and tempest to fall round about without touch the say palace these which thus do be call Tebeth and Chesmir Tebeth and Chesmir two sort of idolater which delude the people with opinion of their sanctity impute these work to their dissemble holiness and for this cause they go in filthy and beastly manner not care who see they with dirt on their face never wash nor comb themselves and if any be condemn to death they take dress and eat he which they do not if any die natural they be also call Bachsi bachsi that be of such a religion or order as if one shall say a frier-preacher or Minor and be exceed expert in their devilish Art they cause that the bottle in the hall of the great can do fill the bowl of their own accord which also without man help pass ten pace through the air into the hand of the say can and when he have drink in like sort return to their place these Bachsi sometime resort unto the officer and threaten plague or other misfortune from their idol which to prevent they desire so many mutton with black head and so many pound of incense and to perform their due sacrifice which they according receive and offer on their feast-day sprinkle broth before their idol there be of these great monastery which seem like a small city in some whereof be two thousand monk which shave their head and beard and wear a religious habit and hallow their idol feast with great solemnity of hymn and light some of these may be marry other there be call sensim sensim a order which observe great abstinence and strictness of life in all their life eat nothing but bran which they put in hot water and let it stand till all the white of the meal be take away and then eat it be thus wash these worship the fire and be condemn of the other for heretic because they worship not their idol and will not marry in any case they be shave and wear hempen-garment of black or bright yellow and although they be silk yet will they not alter the colour they sleep on great mat and live the austere life in the world of their astrologer in Cambalu be not few than five thousand Christian catayan and saracen maintain with food and raiment at the great can charge these by their astrolabe foretell of the change of weather mortality war disease etc. and if any enterprise any great work he resort unto they and tell the hour of his nativity by their art be inform of the success they hold the soul to be immortal and according to every man merit in his life to pass into a more noble creature till it be deify or ignoble as to a peasant and then to a dog and so by degree to the vile they show much reverence to their parent to who if any be ungrateful in their necessity there be a office and officer appoint to try and punish the offence in the emperor hall none dare spit but for that purpose carry a little vessel to spit in nor dare any there make any noise or loud talk the tartar be at first very uncharitable to the poor and will curse they say that if God have love they he will have provide for they but after the idolatrous Bachsi have commend alm for a good work there be great provision make for they and every day at least twenty thousand dish of rice mill and Panike by certain officer distribute among they and for this liberality they adore he as a God cingis among his first law enact as say vincentius the punishment of death to be inflict upon offender in those three vice Vincent bel. spec. histor lib. 30. ca. 70. which before time have be most rife among they namely lie adultery and theft of which yet towards other man that be not tartar they make no conscience they be great usurer take ten in the hundred for a month beside use upon use ca. 75. insomuch that a soldier in Georgia which have borrow five hundred piece of coin call Yperpera retain the same five year be constrain to repay seven thousand and a tartarian lady for seven year use of fifty sheep demand seven thousand they be so covetous that though they abound in cattle they will scarce allow any to their own expense while it be sound and good but if it die or be sick they be addict to sodomy or buggery they eat sometime for necessity man flesh sometime to delight themselves and sometime to terrify other reckon it a great glory to have slay many ca. 76. ca. 77. and William bruise a scot from the relation of Anthony Spinola descend of that family in Genua and then ambassador from casghere the crim-tartar into Polonia affirm diverse thing of the tartarian as namely of threescore and ten diverse kingdom of they the name whereof be scarce know to any tartar differ in language and manner but all agree in the tartarian appellation war wander hard and spare diet all sometime subject to the great can now inferior in power as the crim say which know nothing of he but by tradition to the crim or precopite these Precopites abhor drunkenness punish adultery with death steal not from their countryman nor conceal any thing which they find walk not with weapon have few law the interpreter of which be their priest which they great reverence as they do also those of the christian if any thing be not express by law they refer it to that general head whereon hang the law and the prophet to do as man will be do to the sar or emperor sit himself in judgement with the Galga and sultan so they call the prince child and the chancellor with other senator who sentence be first deliver he determine and present execution follow all metal be the sar prerogative except gold which be the turk peculiar he have also the ten of the spoil and of every captive a chekine and if he be of great estate three he receive 5500. ducat a year from the Turk for which he be bind to war upon none but the Muscovite without his leave he bring into the field 150000. horseman leave at home but one man in a house and when the circassian and astracans adjoin their force two hundred thousand it be pain of death not to come they bring with they three month victual which be dry flesh cheese garlic root and a spare horse for food beside a better for service their hair tie to long pole be their banner only the prince receive from the Turk one of silk both horse and man be exceed skilful in swim in pass over large stream they set their saddle and baggage on reed or rush which they tie to diverse horsetaile themselves hold they by the mane and guide they sometime they sit themselves on those rush and sometime they kill and flay some of their horse and turn the inside outward timber they with the rib of the horse and sow they with the hair make boat for transportation they take off the wheel of their cart and set they on rush as aforesaid transport they the spoil be divide in common and every man loss thence make good to conceal any thing be death whether pillage from the enemy or find of their own people d. Fletcher Desc of Russia 19 in the year 1571. they come to Musco and fire the suburb which be of wood burn with such rage that in four hour space it consume the great part of the city be thirty mile or more in compass the ruefulness of this sight be second with a more dismal event the people burn in their house and street and while they seek to fly out of the city they wedge themselves with multitude so fast in the gate which be further from the enemy and the street adjoin as that three rank walk one upon the other head the uppermost tread down those that be low so that there perish at that time as be say by the fire and the press the number of eight hundred thousand people or more the tartar send the ruff a knife as upbraid he this loss and his desperate case therewith to stab himself the cause of this quarrel be the tartar title to Cazan Astracan and Moscow itself which the Moscovite be wont to acknowledge with this homage yearly in the castle of Mosko to give the can or crim horse oat out of his cap himself on foot the crim abide on his horse this homage Basilius change into a tribute of fur which also by his son John be deny hereupon once or twice every year sometime about Whitsuntide but often in harvest he invade the country either in great number if the can himself come or otherwise in few with light border-skirmish their common practice be to make diverse army and draw the ruff to one place to invade another they be all horseman carry nothing but a bow a sheaf of arrow and a falchion sword they be expert rider and shoot as ready backward as forward the morse or noble have armour like the turk the common-people none other then their apparel viz. a black-sheep skin with the wool-side outward in the day time and inward in the night with a cap of the same they have a rule that justice be to be practise but towards their own and therefore will promise any thing when they besiege a city but be once possess of the place perform all manner of hostility when their number be small they make great show with counterfeit shape of man set on horseback in give onset they make a great shout cry together g g God help we they will die rather than yield contrary to the turk custom the chief booty they seek for be store of captive special young boy and girl for which purpose they have band intend nothing else and basket like baker Pannyer to carry they tender if they tire or sicken on the way they dash they against the ground or some tree and so leave they dead the ruff border be use to their invasion keep few other cattle but swine which their religion abhor to touch they differ herein from the turkish religion their image that they have certain idol puppet make of silk or like stuff of the fashion of a man which they fasten to the door of their walking-house to be as januss or keeper of their house and these idol be make not by all but by certain religious woman which they have among they for that and like use they have beside the image of their king of a huge bigness which they erect at every stage when the army march to which every one must bow as he pass by both tartar and stranger they be much give to witchcraft and ominous conjecture in marriage they only abstain from the mother sister and daughter neither do they account that woman a wife which have not honour they with the name of a father and then begin he to take a dowry of her friend of horse sheep kine etc. if she be barren after a certain time he turn she home again under the emperor they have certain duke or Morseys which rule over hoard of ten twenty or forty thousand which be bind to serve the emperor with a certain number of man double-horsed they prefer horseflesh before other meat esteem it strong nourishment this notwithstanding they use to send thirty or forty thousand horse yearly to Musko to exchange for other commodity their herd of kine and flock of black sheep they keep rather for the milk than the flesh though they sometime eat it they drink milk or warm blood and for the most part cure they both together as they travel they sometime let their horse blood and drink it from his body town they plant none not stand village but have walk house build upon wheel like a shepherd cottage which they move in the spring from the south to the north and so with winter return southwards when they come to their stage or stand place plant their house in a rank make the form of a town and street gold and silver they neglect as they do also tillage which free their country from invasion for person and complexion they have broad and flat visage of a tan colour into yellow and black fierce and cruel look thin haired upon the upper lip and pit of the chin light and nimble body with short leg practise themselves to ride and shoot from their childhood their parent not suffer their child to eat till they have shoot within a certain scantling of the mark their speech be sudden and loud as it be out of a deep hollow throat their sing like a cow low in the description of these Crim I have be thus long because they be now the chief know nation of the wander tartar and the rest differ little from they except in great barbarism carry home to their house and assemble their kinsfolk eat it with great reverence and rejoice save the bone in goodly vessel the priest have for their fee the head foot innards skin and some part of the flesh when any of great place die they b b funeral observance in sabion assemble the astrologer and tell the hour of his nativity that they may by their art find a planet fit to the burn of the corpse which sometime in this respect attend this fiery constellation a week a month or half a year in all which time they set before the corpse a table furnish with bread wine and other viand leave they there so long as one may convenient eat they the spirit there present in their opinion refresh himself with the odour of this provision if any evil happen to any of the house the astrologer ascribe it to the angry soul for neglect of his due hour agree to that of his nativity they make many stay by the way wherein they present this depart soul with such cate to hearten it against the Igha Igha Igha to which the priest with his voice reply and they answer he with the self same word so many time till in the end he become as it be mad fall down as he be dead have nothing on he but a which they call dibananguin and atazanguin that be Levant and ponent or under the wind west and beyond the wind east all the navigation in those part be by the monsoon or certain wind which observe their set season of the year in those time reign in Cingapura one Sangesinga and in the neighbour part of java one Paraerisae who die leave to the care of his brother his two son which slay the elder and make himself king by his tyranny cause diverse of the javan nobility to forsake their country among the rest Paramisora flee to Cingapura who with his many follower be entertain kind by Sangesinga who not long after he ungrateful slay and by the help of his javan possess himself of the state the king of siam who tributary and son-in-law Sangesinga have be force he to leave his ill get throne and to seek new habitation one hundred and forty mile thence where he settle himself at the river Muar with two thousand follower some of which be call Cellati man that live on the sea by fish and piracy these he will not receive into his new fortress of Pago as not well trust they though before they had make he lord of Cingapura these therefore seat themselves fifteen mile from Muar in the place near which malaca now stand join with the native half savage who language be call Malayan the place grow straight they remove three mile up the river where be a hill call Beitan with a large plain the commodiousness whereof invite Paramisora to leave Pago and to join with they in this new foundation which be after call malaca signify a banish man in remembrance of this javan exile in Andrea Corsuli affirm the same thing of their Pythagorean error and add that they sometime buy fowl or other beast of the portugal which mean to have dress they and let they fly or run away in the highway also and wood they set pot with water and cast corn or other grain upon the ground to feed the bird and beast and to omit their charitable hospital before mention if they take a flea or a louse they will not kill it but put it in some hole or corner in the wall and so let it go and you can do they no great injury then to kill it in their presence which with all entreaty they will resist as be a heinous sin to take away the life of that to which God have impart both soul and body and where word will not prevail they will offer money they eat no radish onion garlic or any kind of herb that have red colour in it nor egg for they think there be blood in they they drink not wine nor use vinegar but only water they will rather starve then eat with any but their countryman as it happen when I sail from goa to cochin with they in a Portugal ship when they have spend all their store the timefalling out long than they make account of they will not once touch our meat they wash themselves every time they eat or ease themselves or make water under their hair they have a star upon their forehead which they rub every morning with a little white Sanders temper with water and three or four grain of rice among it which the Bramenes also do as a superstitious ceremony of their law they sit on the ground in their house upon mat or carpet and so they eat leave their shoe which be pike and hook at the door for the which cause the heel of their shoe be seldom pull up to save labour of undo they the moor 10 10 od. Barbosa among they will sometime abuse the superstition of these cambayan to their own covetousness bring some worm rat or sparrow and threaten to kill the same so to provoke they to redeem the life thereof at some high price and likewise if a malefactor be condemn to death they will purchase his life of the magistrate and sell he for a slave the moor will sometime make semblance as if they will kill themselves that these foolish guzzarate may see they in like sort they will go out of the path if they light on a anthill lest they may happy tread on some of they they sup by daylight lest their candlelight shall occasion the death of some gnat or Fly and when they must needs use a candle they keep it in a lantern for that cause if louse do much annoy they they call to they certain religious and holy man after their account and these observant y y the like lousy trick be report in the Legend of s. Francis and in the life of Ignatius of one of the first jesuitical pillar by Maffaeus will take upon they all those louse which the other can find and put they on their head there to nourish they but yet for all this lousy scruple they stick not at cozenage by false weight measure and coin nor at usury and lie some be say z z n. di cont. to be so zealous in their Idol-service as to sacrifice their life in their honour whereunto they be persuade by the preach of their priest as the most acceptable devotion many offer themselves which be bring upon a scaffold after certain ceremony put about his neck a iron collar round without but within very sharp from which hang a chain down his breast into which sit down he put his foot and while the priest mutter certain word the party before the people with all his force stretch out his foot and cut off his head their reward be that they be account saint chap. 9 of the indian nation betwixt Cambaia and malabar and their religion @. i. of the season of the year and of the part next to Cambaya the mighty river of Indus and Ganges pay their fine to the lord of water the ocean almost under the very Tropic of cancer do as it be betwixt their watery arm present into that their mother bosom this large chersonesus a country full of kingdom riches people and our dew task superstitious custom as Italy be divide by the apennine and bound by the Alpes so be this by the hill which they call gate which go from east to west but not direct and quite thorough to the cape comori which not only have enter league with many in-lets of the sea to divide the soil into many signiory and kingdom but with the air and nature high officer to dispense with the ordinary order and establish statue of nature a a gi. bot. ben. maff. lib. 1. Linschot lib. 1. cap. 34. jarric l. 3. c. 1. at the same time under the same elevation of the sun divide to summer and winter their season and possession for whereas cold be banish out of these country except on the top of some hill and altogether prohibit to approach so near the court and presence of the sun and therefore their winter and summer be not reckon by heat and cold but by the fairness and foulness of weather which in those part divide the year by equal proportion at the same time when on the west-part of this Peninsula between that ridge of mountain and the sea it be after their appellation summer which be from September till April in which time it be always clear sky without once or very little rain on the other side the hill which they call the coast of Choromandell it be their winter every day and night yield abundance of rain beside those terrible thunder which both begin and end their winter and from April till September in a contrary vicissitude on the western part be winter and on the eastern summer insomuch that in little more than twenty league journey in some place as where they cross the hill to saint Thomas on the one side of the hill you ascend with a fair summer on the other you descend attendant with a stormy winter the like say Linschoten happen at the cape Rosalgate in Arabia and in many other place of the east their winter also Transil observe many ceremony in kill a hog in sacrifice as it seem to the sun after the sound of their cymbal and certain cate set down in platter two old woman come forth with trumpet or pipe of reed and do reverence to the sun and then clothe themselves with sacred vestment one of they put about her forehead a hairlace with two horn hold another heir-lace or scarf in her hand and so begin to sound dance and call upon the sun wherein she be follow by the other both of they in this manner dance about the hog which be there fast tie the horn beldame still mutter certain word to the sun and the other answer she then do she take a cup of wine and after some ceremony pour it on the hog and after that with a lance after dance and flourish she kill the hog all this while a little torch be burn which at last she take into her mouth and bite it and the other woman wash the pipe with the swine blood and with her finger imbrue with blood mark the forehead of her husband first and then of the rest then do they untire themselves and only with woman associate eat the cheer in the platter and after singe the hog and eat he without these ceremony they eat no swine flesh from hence Magellan go to Mathan where in a battle with the islander he be shine in pulaoan they keep cock for the game but eat not of their flesh forbid by their superstition in Ciumbubon they find a tree which have leaf like those of the mulberry have beside on each side of the leaf as it be two foot with which as if it have be move and sensible it will stir and go up and down Pigafetta keep one eight day in a platter and when he touch it present it will flee from he and move up and down he think it live of the air in Burneo the people be partly moores and partly gentile and according to their religion have two king and two royal city situate in salt-water the moor when they kill a hen or a goat use first certain word to the sun the gentile o o Mas. hither from java China and malacca they profess Mahometism so devout that they never go to their watch before they have pray in the whereinto they enter be first wash after the Mahometan manner but pray so loud that they may be hear a great distance their word of prayer be Stofferolla Stofferolla Ascehad a Ascehad a Ylla Ascehad a ill lolla ill lolla mahume die Rosulla at the pronounce of which banquet in their temple very often every one bring his part of the cheer which sometime they do in the wood a hundred in a company at these time they consult of public affair they have civil war nera and lantoor hold together against three other town two little island Polleruijn and Poelvunay take part with nera Polerine or Poolaroon and Polaway and when occasion require come thither with their boat to consultation where they be entertain in public feast the manner whereof be that they sit down in order in stead of a table every one have a piece of a leaf of the banana tree then be set before each a piece of Sagu bread after that a dish make of the leaf of another tree with a little sodden rice and flesh-pottage which they hurl by handful into their mouth devour rather then eat the same in the meanwhile the gentleman arise with their weapon and exercise themselves in martial game with dance the quarrel betwixt these islander grow about the cut of certain tree from whence it be come to cut and kill one another with cruel butchery they exercise sea-fight in their or galeot with great dexterity with great shout and cry the gentleman dance on the hatch very active they be very bloody and barbarous yet bury the head of their enemy with sweet odour if any of their friend die the woman make a shrill and loud cry to call he again which not effect they provide a great feast whereunto all the kindred and friend be invite they bury they almost after our fashion in a white sheet the corpse be carry on man shoulder the man first and woman after follow a censer be there leave fume all the day and might and in the night they keep a light burn in a little house which they have set over the grave in the morning and evening all of all sort come and say their prayer a long while together at the grave and be ask wherefore they say that the dead shall not arise again they have a play with the ball exercise by many of they not as among we with the hand but with their foot the world as the body of little man happy the only true pigmy the world yield in samara the three of those kingdom none of the North-star can be see they be man-eater and idolater but not so brutish as in dragorian the next kingdom where if a man be sick his kinsman consult with their sorcerer who inquire of the devil whether he shall escape or no and if the answer be negative they send for certain man special design to that villainous mystery which strangle he and then they dress and eat he among the kindred even to the very marrow in his bone for say they if any flesh shall remain it will putrify and worm will breed thereof which after for want of sustenance will perish whereby the soul of the dead party will be much torment the bone they bury safe that no beast shall touch they such dread have they of beast and cruelty in a more than beastly cruelty and such a care to observe humanity and piety in a most impious inhumanity Lambri the next kingdom have in it some man with tail like dog a span long the last be Fanfur where they live of bread make of pith of tree the wood whereof be heavy and sink to the bottom if it be put in water like iron and therefore they make Candish Hak. tom. 3. pag. 822. be mention make of a javan king call Raia Ballomboam very age m m Houtman say he be alive 1596. suppose 160. year old which have a hundred wife and his son have fifty their custom be that when the king die they burn the body and preserve the ash five day after the wife of the dead king go to a place appoint and there she which be dear in his favour throw a ball from she and where that ball rest thither they go all and turn their face eastward stab themselves with a Crise or dagger to the heart they be very resolute people and dread no attempt which the king shall enjoin they be it never so dangerous all the race of this king Ballomboam be raze and utter destroy by the Passaruan after a long siege which war be begin in the blood of the king of ballamboam daughter who he slay as be before say and add this drunkenness unto his thirst jortam or n n Navig Oliver Noort joartam contain about a thousand household the inhabitant be ethnic and have their great in all those part he be a hundred and twenty year old and have many wife which nourish he with their milk be not able to take other sustenance a deadly enemy to the christian who the king do yet with some privilege favour Edmund Scot write that they use in Bantam martial law adultery be death The free javan must to every wife keep ten women-slave which be their concubine also some keep forty but they may have but three wife they be proud and by this multitude of slave poor cruel and cowardly their criss or dagger be two foot long wave indenture-fashion and poison that few escape the vulgar sort have little religion but many pray to the devil who for that end they have paint in their house and set wax candle and sing before they for fear of hurt which they do not to God because of his goodness the most of their work be to carve stick for their Criss-handles they be couzener thief idle glutton take Betele opium tobacco they have diverse Sect yet most be in manner atheist many Chinois dwell there some think that if they be good they shall be bear again after death to great riches and that wicked man shall be turn into toad or other ugly beast every new moon they burn sacrifice and sing over they certain prayer in the mean while tinge a bell which at the end of every prayer they ring out which be also their passing-bell ceremony when any be ready to die they the christian captive rest only upon friday and eight other day in the year festival to the moor there be six hundred fountain wall about the water whereof be convey by conduit to the temple or other place because the river be sometime dry they have in Fez a judge for criminal cause and another for question of religion a three that deal in matrimonial case from these there lie a appeal to the high advocate the judge of Mahomet law in matter of conscience have no allowance for the same their marriage be thus when the father of the maid have espouse she to her a a the man never see his bride before marriage but send his mother or some other woman to see she and upon that report agree with the father lover they go with their friend to church and have with they two notary which draw the covenant agree betwixt they into write the father bestow a dowry or portion of money apparel and such like seldom of land when the bridegroom fetch she home she be set in a cabinet cover with silk and carry by porter accompany with her kinsfolk and much minstrelsy and the Bridegroom friend go before with torch and her kinsman after towards the great church then he haste home expect his bride in his chamber who her father brother and uncle bring and deliver to his mother and he set his foot on she shue the chamber door at which a woman stand and receive of he a napkin stain which she show to the assembly as a testimony of the bride virginity but if she be not find a maid she be return to he friend with shame and the guest go home without their feast they hold great feast also at the circumcision of their male-child which be the seven day after they be bear the barber or circumciser be present with gift of all the invite guest then follow mirth and jollity they use dance but the woman apart by themselves without man there be a remainder of holiday institute by the christian which themselves understand not on Christmas even they eat a salad make of diverse herb and seethe all kind of pulse which they feed upon on newyear day the child go with mask on their face to the house of gentleman and have fruit give they for sing certain song on the feast of saint John Baptist they use to make bonfire they make a feast call Dentista when their child tooth begin to grow unto other child when a man die the woman put on sackcloth and defile their face with dirt they call to they those wicked man in woman attire which have foursquare drum to the sound whereof they sing mournful ditty in praise of the dead party at the end of every verse the woman utter most hideous shriek and out-cry tear their hair and beat their breast and cheek till they be all imbrue with blood and thus they continue seven day and then intermit their mourn forty day after which space they resume the same for three day as before but the better sort behave themselves more modest at this time all the widow friend come about she to comfort she and send her diverse kind of meat for in the mourning-house they may dress no meat at all till the dead be carry out the woman which lose her father brother or husband never go forth with the funeral at some festival the youth of one street will fight with club against the boy of another street and sometime betake they to other weapon and kill one another sometime they use these bloody fray without the city the officer force they to better order there be many poet which pen amorous sonnet and on Mahomet birthday make verse in his commendation resort early to the palace and there ascend the tribunal read their verse to the people and he who verse be best be pronounce that year prince of poet the marin king on that day use to entertain the learned man and to reward the best poet with a hundred ducat a horse a woman-slave and the king robe which he wear that day in Fez be two hundred grammar school build like great hals every day they learn one lesson of the Alcoran they read and write not in book but in great b b these table be board like Horn-book when one lesson be learn that be wipe out and another write and so throughout the Alcoran till all be learned table in seven year they learn the whole Alcoran by heart and then the father invite his son schoolfellow to a banquet and his son ride through the street in costly apparel both which be lend by the governor the other boy ride and sing song in praise of God and Mahumet on Mahomet birthday every boy must carry a torch to school curious wrought some weigh thirty pound which they light before day and let they burn till sunrising sing all the while the praise of Mahumet the schoolmaster have the remnant of the wax which sometime they sell for a hundred ducat they be free school ancient build in the school and also in the college they have two day of recreation every week wherein they neither teach nor study @. 3 of their diviner and sect and other part of the fezan Territorie there be three kind of fortune-teller or diviner one of which use Geomantical figure other pour a drop of oil into a glass of water which become clear as a Seeing-glass in which they say they see strange sight rank of devil like army some travel some pass over a river etc. when the divine seethe they quiet he demand such question of they as he will and the devil with gesture return answer the three sort be women-witche which make the people believe that they be acquaint with devil of diverse sort red white black and when they will tell any man fortune they perfume themselves with certain odour whereby as they say the devil enter into they and their voice be present alter as if the devil speak within they and then they that come to inquire ask their question and so have leave their present for the devil depart these a a a female filthiness woman use unlawful lust between themselves in mutual filthiness and if fair woman come to they they will demand the devil fee that they may have such deal with they yea some addict themselves to these abominable practice will feign themselves sick and send to one of these witch which will affirm that she be possess with a devil and can be cure except she become one of their society the foolish husband believe consent and make a sumptuous feast at her devilish admission other will conjure this devil with a cudgel out of their wife other feign themselves to be possess with a devil will deceive the witch as they have deceive their wife there be exorcist or diviner call Muhazzimi which cast out devil or if they can they excuse themselves and say it be a airy spirit they write the one shall be call conserver the other reformer of the Law after the tartar have sack Bagdat in the year of the Hegeira 656. these sectary swarm all over Asia and Africa they will admit none into belly-cheer be the cause for one of they will eat as much as will serve three or else it be through wicked lust for sometime one of the principal with all his disciple be invite to some marriage-feast hermit among these sect in Fez be some rule esteem heretical of both sort of doctor some hold that a man by good work fast and abstinence may attain to the nature of a angel the understanding and heart be thereby so purify say they that a man can sin though he will but to this height be ascend by fifty step of discipline and though they fall into sin before they come into the fifty degree yet will not God impute it they use strange and incredible fast in the beginning but after take all the pleasure of the World they have a severe form of live set down in four book by a by a certain Elfargano comment on the same and thence gather the rule and the degree aforesaid in three hundred year none have write more elegant verse which therefore they use in all their banquet they hold that the heaven element planet and star be one God and that no religion be erroneous because every one take that which he worship for God they think that all knowledge of God be contain in one man call Elcorb elect by God and wise as he forty among they be call Elauted which signify block of these be elcoth or Elcorb elect when the former be dead threescore and ten elector make the choice there be circle and enchant by his charm all the serpent thereabouts thereinto and then kill that which seem to he most venomous let the rest go with the blood thereof and the seed of a certain tree he temper a poison for that purpose with which a weapon infect draw never so little blood do kill in a quarter of a hour they have great store of parrot which be instruct by a marvelous natural cunning to prevent the serpent which will else destroy their nest they build therefore on high tree and on the end of some tender bough thereof they fasten a bulrush which hang down two span thereunto weave and work their nest in such sort that the serpent for fear of fall dare not adventure to deal therewith the negro come about Cadamosto with wonder to see his apparel and the whiteness of his colour never before have they see any Christian and some of they with spital rub his skin to see whether his whiteness be natural or no which perceive it to be no tincture they be out of measure astonish they will then give nine or sometime fourteen slave for a horse furnish and when they buy a horse they will bring some of their enchanter which make a fire of herb and set the horse over the smoke utter certain word and after that anoint he with a thin ointment and shut he up twenty day that none may see he hang certain trumpery about his neck think that hereby they be more secure in battle gun seem to they for their hideous noise to be of the devil lag-pipe they think to be a live creature that thus sing in variable accent but when they be suffer to handle they they think they to be some heavenly thing that God have make with his own hand to sound so sweet they behold the ship with great curiosity and eye that be carve in the prow of the ship they take to be eye indeed by which it see how to direct the course at sea they say the christian that can thus make voyage by sea be great enchanter and comparable to the devil themselves have enough to do to travel by land see a candle burn in the night they which know not to make any light but their fire esteem it wonderful honey they have which they suck out of the comb but the wax they hurl away till they be instruct how to make candle thereof g description of Guinea tree be always green some have leaf twice a year they seldom see the sun either rise or go down by the space of half of a hour their winter begin in April which yet be their time of harvest maize be bring thither out of America in April May and june they have much rain and the same very dangerous to the body and rot the clothes if it be not present dry the creature in Guinea it be often as warm as if it be sodden they have some snake thirty foot long as much as six man can carry they have also a beast like a crocodile call Lanhadi we have speak of the like about Pegu and Bengala which never go into the water spider as big as the palm of one hand which do not spin store of cameleon dog woolly with sharp snout of diverse colour which can bark drive to the market as sheep tie one to another blue parrot many sort of ape black fly which seem to burn in Senega some snake have mouth so wide that they a whole sheep without tear they have wing dragon with tail and long mouth with many tooth be blue and green which some negro worship they boar a hole in the Palm-wine tree whence issue a white juice first sweet and after by stand it become sour and after by stand it become sour it be somewhat like the coco-tree the Palmita be without branch the fruit grow on the top which within be like pomegranate full of grain without of a golden colour they buy gentility with gift a dog a sheep a cow in their creation be observe much solemnity they know not how to number their year but seem to live long in their winter they have much sickness and mortality the good of the decease descend not to his child but to the brethren if he have any otherwise to his father if it be a woman her husband deliver her marriage good to her brethren when the king die the the child new bear have a clean cloth wrap about the middle and be lay down on a mat the mother use to bear their child at their back and so travel with they none prove lame notwithstanding that shake of their body they give they the breast over their shoulder when it be a month old they hang a net about the body like a shirt education of their child make of the bark of a tree hang full of fetish to secure it from the devil who otherwise will they think carry it away they hang the hair full of shell and coral about the neck arm and leg apply fetish or wreathe with superstitious fancy that one be good against vomit a second for fall a three for bleed a four to make it sleep a five against wild beast and so on in the rest give to each Fetisso a several name they quick learn they to eat and then leave they about the house like dog they soon learn to go to speak to swim when they be first bear they be not black but reddish as the brasilian each woman bring up her own they teach they no civility and beat they sometime cruel with staff when they be eight or ten or twelve year old they learn they to spin bark-threed and make net after that they go with their father to fish at eighteen year old they begin to set up for themselves two or three of they together hire a house and Canoa and then they cover their privity grow amorous and their father look out wife for they they have little hair on their face at thirty they wear nail as long as the joint of a man finger as a token of gentility which be also observe by merchant they keep they very clean and as white as ivory they be great in flesh beyond man of these part at threescoore and ten or fourscore their blackness decay and they grow yellow they have small belly long leg broad foot long toe sharp sight quick wit themselves of purpose they wear bead about their neck and straw fetish about their foot the Mulato woman in mina cut their hair short for bravery their ornament they cut three gash on their forehead a black silk doublet cut and pink they have earing and bracelet of copper the unmarried maid wear thirty or forty on each arm of iron the common quean wear copper ring with bell on their leg these woman be strong nimble well proportion good housewife home-keeper and cook not very fruitful the riches of the guinean be store of wife and child they take great pride of white tooth which therefore they rub with a certain wood they show like ivory their garment be a fathom or more of linen cloth which they wear about their body from beneath the breast to the knee upon which they gird a piece of blue or yellow cloth whereon hang their knife and key and diverse wispe of straw or fetish when they go to market they wash they from top to toe and put on other clothes they buy no more but for that day or meal they stamp their Milia as we do spice fan it in a wooden dish steep it overnight with a little maize and in the morning lay it on a stone and as painter their colour grind it with another stone till it be down which they temper with fresh water and salt and make roll thereof twice as big as a man fist and bake it a little on the hearth this be their bread their bread their diet their diet be strange as raw flesh handful of grain large draught of aquavitae dog cat buffle elephant though stink like carrion and a thousand maggot creep in they there be little bird like bulfinche which make their nest on small end of twig for fear of snake these they eat alive with their feather the moor say that within land they eat dry snake and these will eat dog gut raw which our author have see and a boy leave in pawn on shipbord for debt which have meat enough yet will secret kill the hen that he may eat their raw gut they will eat old stink fish dry in the sun yet can they be dainty if they may have it some make a kind of ale of maize and water sod together call poitou sometime four or five together will buy a pot of Palm-wine which they pour into a great Cabas which grow on tree and some of they be half as big as a kilderkin drink round about which they sit to drink each send a little potful to his best wife when they first drink they take it out with a small Cabas and lay arm and leg otherwise think they can not drink in quiet they be great drinker and feed as unmannerly as swine sit on the ground and cram not stay till the morsel in the mouth be swallow but tear their meat in piece with the three mid-finger cast it into their mouth ready gape to receive it they be always hungry and will eat all day long yea the dutchman have great stomach while they be there he that get most must be most liberal industrious to get and as prodigal in spend upon their liquor before the portugal trade they have no merchandise but go naked and the people within land be afraid of they because they be white and apparel they come to trade in the ship in the morning see wind for about noon the wind before blow from land come from sea and they be not able to endure the roughness thereof they believe that man when they die go into another world where they shall have like need of many thing as here they have and therefore use to put with the dead corpse some part of household and if they lose any thing they think that some of their friend which in the other world have need thereof come thence and steal it of * * the religion of the guinean God be ask they say he be black and evil and do then much harm their good they have by their own labour and not by his goodness circumcision they use and some other turkish rite they hold it unmeet and irreligious to spit on the ground they have no letter nor book they observe a sabbath Tuesday Sabbath they call it dio fetish herein agree and yet disagree with Turk jew and Christian for they observe Tuesday rest from their fish and husbandry the wine of the palmtree which be that day gather may not be sell but be offer to the king who bestow it on his courtier to drink at night in the midst of the marketplace they have a table stand on four pillar two elf high who flat cover be make straw and reed weave together hereon be set many straw ring call fetish or God and therein wheat with water and oil for their god which they think eat the same their priest they call Fetissero who every festival day place a seat on that table and sit thereon preach to the people the content whereof I can never learn which do the woman offer he their infant and he sprinkle they with water in which a newt or snake do swim and then besprinkle the table aforesaid with the same water and so utter certain word very loud and stroke the child with certain colour as give they his blessing he drink of that water the people clap their hand and cry 1. i. and so he dismiss his devout assembly many wear such ring of straw next their body as preservative from those danger which else their angry god may inflict on they in honour of the same deity or devil as it seem they conceive he to be they bechalke themselves with a kind of chalkey earth and this be unto they in stead of their morning matin the first bit at meal and first draught be consecrate to their idol and therefore they besprinkle therewith those ring which I say they wear on their body if fisher can speed at sea they give a piece of gold to the Fetissero to reconcile their frown saint he therefore with his wife walk a kind of procession through the city smite his breast and clap his hand with a mighty noise till he come at the shore and there they cut down certain bough from the tree and hang they on their neck and play on a timbrel then do the Fetissero turn to his wife and expostulate with they and withal hurl into the sea wheat and other thing as a offering to Fetisso to appease his displeasure towards the fisherman when the king will sacrifice to Fetisso he command the Fetissero to inquire of a tree whereto he ascribe divinity what he will demand he with his wife come to the tree and in a heap of ash there provide prick in a branch pluck off certain fish to their canonization in this respect they take not the tunny at all the swordfish they take but eat not till his sword be cut off which be dry and hold in great veneration the mountain will bend their sullen brow if they shall not have some red letter in their calendar to which their top aspire threaten to scale heaven or overwhelm the earth if the Fetissan portion do not pacify Fetisso and the party decease be now at rest in the mean time the dear of his wife fill all the house with mourn the neighbour and friend with song and music such as they have and dance and at last apparel the rich buy it of the moor attire themselves after their fashion the rest both man and woman use a skin or some course piece of linen without adorn by art when they do reverence to any they cast off this cloth from their shoulder to the navel strip themselves half naked they wear their hair long which serve they for a hat or head attire and for great neatness and gallantry they curl it in diverse manner and anoint it with butter which in the sun show like dew on the grass so curious be they herein that for fear of disorder their curl they have a crotch fasten in the earth whereon at night they lay their neck and so sleep with their head hang they brand themselves on the whole body special on the face the nail of their little finger they suffer to grow to the great length imitate as much as may be the spur of cock which also they sometime fasten and fit to their finger their hand and foot which common be bare they die reddish with the juice of a certain bark n. Godig l. 1. c. 12. they be a slothful people scarce provide necessary for life not give themselves to hunt or fish and although the material of woollen linen cotton be at hand yet do the most of they of the word Umbare which signify a threefooted stool on which each of they sit some on the right other on the left hand in the town the lord be judge where when any one sue the lord send one of his servant to the defendant assign he a time to make his appearance and then the plaintiff and defendant plead each his own case this be the fashion in Barbary also and many other place and after they have both say what they can all that be present give sentence from this they may appeal to the Umbares from they to the azage or supreme judge and from these to the emperor sometime justice itinerant in war or kill their enemy they observe a more than beastly testimony of their great valour which be after this manner they cut off their privy member to deprive they of all hope of generation and then dry they well for preservation after which they come before the king with great reverence in the presence of the principal man of the village and there take these member so dry one by one in their mouth and spit they on the ground at the king foot which the king with great thanks accept and the more to honour they cause they all to be take up and give to they again which be from trial of controversy * * this trial be call Motamba for which purpose they lay a kind of hatchet which they have in the fire and the ganga-mokisso or mokisso priest take the same red hot and draw it near to the skin of the accuse party and if there be two he cause their leg to be set near together and draw this hot iron without touch between they if it burn that party be condemn as guilty way down undermine and make spacious within and there set he on a seat of earth with his bead which they use in chain and bracelet for ornament and the most part of his good with he in his last home
