the manner of the hebrew like as also the rest of the nation of those country use to be they have abundance of elephant and wear clothes of palm Andrew b b Andrew bat. battle live among they two year and a half they be say he heathen and observe many superstition they have their mokisso or image to which they offer according to the proportion of their sort and suit the fisher offer fish when he sue for his help in his fish the countryman wheat the weaver alibungo piece of cloth other bring bottle of wine all want that they will have and bring what they want furnish their Mokisso with those thing whereof they complain themselves to be disfurnish their ceremony for the dead be diverse they bring goat and let they bleed at the mokisso foot which they after consume in a feast memorial of the decease party which be continue four or five day together and that four or five several time in the year by all of his friend and kindred the day be know and though they dwell twenty mile the end yet they will resort to these memorial-exequies and beginning in the night will sing doleful and funeral song till day and then kill as aforesaid and make merry the hope of this make such as have store of friend to contemn death and the want of friend to bewail he make a man conceive a more dreadful apprehension of death their conceit be so ravish with superstition that many die of none other death kin be the name of unlawful and prohibit meat which according to each kindred devotion to some family be some kind of fish to another a hen to another a buff and so of the rest in which they observe their vow abstinence so strict that if any shall though at unaware eat of this kin he will die of conceit always present to his accuse conscience the breach of his vow and the anger of Mokisso he have know diverse thus to have die and sometime will when some of they have eat with he make they believe that they have eat of their kin till have sport himself with their superstitious agony he will affirm the contrary they use to set in their field and place where corn or fruit grow a basket with Goats-horn parrot feather and other trash this be the mokisso ensign or token that it be commend to his custody and therefore the people very much addict to theft dare not meddle or take any thing likewise if a man weary with his burden lay it down in the highway and knit a knot of grass and lay thereon or leave any other note know to they to testify that he have leave it there in the name of his idol it be secure from the lime-finger of any passenger conceit will kill the man that shall transgress in this kind in the Banza or chief city the chief idol be name chekoke every day they have there market and the chekoke be bring forth by the Ganga or priest to keep good rule and be set in the marketplace to prevent steal moreover the king have a bell c c recovery of steal good the stroke whereof sound such terror into the heart of the fearful thief that none dare keep any steal good after the sound of that bell. our author inhabit in a little reed-house after the Loango manner and have hang by the wall in a cloth-case his piece wherewith he use to shoot fowl for the king which more for love of the cloth then for the piece be steal upon complaint this bell in form like a Cowbell be carry about and ring with proclamation to make restitution and he have his piece the next morning set at his door the like another find in a bag of bead of a hundred pound weight steal from he and recover by the sound of this bell. they have a dreadful and deadly kind of trial in controversy after this manner a a trial of suspect person there be a little tree or shrub with a small root be call Imbunda about the bigness of one thumb half a foot long like a white carrot now when any list to accuse a man or family or whole street of the death of any of his friend say that such a man bewitch he the Ganga assemble the accuse party and scrape that root the scrape whereof he mix with water which make it as bitter as gall he taste of it one root will serve for the trial of a hundred man the Ganga brew the same together in gourd and with plantine stalk hit every one after they have drink with certain word those that have receive the drink walk by till they can make urine and then they be thereby free other abide till either urine tree they or dizziness take they which the people no soon perceive but they cry Undoke Undoke that be naughty witch and he be no soon fall by his dizziness but they knock he on the head and drag he away hurl he over the cliff in every liberty they have such trial which they make in case of theft and death of any person every week it fall out that some or other undergo this trial which consume multitude of people there be certain person call dunda which be bear of negro-parent and yet be by some unknown cause white they be very rare and when such happen to be bear they be bring to the king and become great witch they be his councillor and advise he of lucky and unlucky day for execution of his enterprise when the king go any whither the dundas go with he and beat the ground round about with certain exorcism before the wherein be a image call Morumba who religion extend far they be swear to this religion at ten or twelve year old but for probation be first put in a house where they have hard diet and must be mute for nine or ten day any provocation to speak notwithstanding then do they bring he before Morumba and prescribe he his kin or perpetual abstinence from some certain meat they make a cut in his shoulder like to a half moon and sprinkle the blood at morumbas foot and swear he to that religion in the wound they put a certain white powder in token of his late admission which so long as it continue do privilege he to take his meat and drink with whosoever he please none deny he the same at free cost they also have their fatal trial before this image where the accuse party kneel down and TEneriffe be the pleasant of the canary island this island have be call nivaria by reason of the snow which like a collar environ the neck of the pike of teyda the name of Tenariffe be impose by the inhabitant of the palm island for Tener in the palmesian language signify snow and a Hill it be situate in the Atlantic ocean fourscore league from the coast of Africa it be in form triangular extend itself into three cape and stand within eight and twenty degree of the equinoctial the great mountain of teyda common call the pike of Tenariffe be a mountain which beget I know not whether a great attention when you come to it or when you behold from a far off but in both very great the base of it begin at the port-town of garachico journey up though pike and description thereof from whence it be two day journey and a half to the top of it the point of which though it seem as sharp as a sugarloaf which figure of all other it do most resemble yet be there a flat of a acre in breadth on the top of it and in the midst of that flat a gulf out of which great stone be with like noise fire and smoke many time cast forth a Vulcan seven league off this way may be travel upon ass or mule the rest on foot and with great difficulty all the country lie about the ascent of the hill for ten mile upward be overgrow or rather adorn with the goodly tree in the world of diverse sort goodly country by reason of the multitude of spring which intermingle one with another and with the addition of the violent winter rain descend in huge torrent down into the sea a cold ascent and hot top and bottom in the midst of this hill be the cold intolerable in the top the heat and so likewise in the bottom through all the cold region you must cast your journey to travel on the south side and in the day time through all the hot region which be within two league of the top on the north side and in the night time every man carry his own portion of victual and borrachoc of wine your time of approach to the top must be about midsummer for the avoid of the torrent cause by the snow and about two of the clock in the morning and so you may abide there until sunrising but no long the sun be exalt above the horizon of the ocean seem far less than when you be on the low ground and seem to whirl itself about in manner of a gyre rarity of the sun hot breath the stream that come out of the east a little before his rise can be compare to nothing more proper then to the breath of a hot oven and so come on his course through a unclouded heaven be of a pure blue crystalline colour without the least spot in it when you be on the top of this hill all the island lie subject like a plain and level plot of ground under you although there be in this island not so few as twenty thousand sharp deform and uneven rock cloud beneath they no wind not rain and all the edge of that plain ground seem to be lift or fringe with snow which indeed be nothing else but the white cloud which be many furlong below you near the top of this mountain it never reign neither be there ever any wind stir thereupon the same be report of the hill Olympus all the upper part of this mountain be afflict with barrenness want the generative benefit of the low and middle region of the air for no manner of tree bald and barren shrub or leaf beautify the head thereof but it rest disgrace with a unseemly baldness out of which towards the south side do the vein of Brimstone issue down into the neck thereof where the region of snow be among which the brimstone be intervene in diverse place in the summer time the fire fire do ofter break forth from out the hole in the top of this hill into which if you throw a great stone it sound as if a great weight have fall upon infinite store of hollow brass the spaniard merry call it the devil cauldron devil cauldron wherein the whole provision of hell be boil but the natural the guanche themselves do say that it be hell and that the soul of their wicked ancestor go thither to be torment conceit of Hell and that those who be good and valiant man go down into the pleasant valley where the great city di laguna laguna now stand then which and the town adjoin to it there be not in any place of the world a more delicater temperature of air nor a goodly object for the eye to make a royal landscape of as to stand in the centre of this plain and to behold how nature have delineate all earthly beauty in the great on the north side of the island be many fresh water with fall down from the top of exceed high mountain refresh the plain and city di laguna and be afterward by the greatness of their torrent carry into the ocean the island be part in the midst with a ridge of mountain like the roof of a church have in the midst of it like a steeple the pike of teyda rock if you divide the island into twelve part ten of they be take up in impassable rocky hill in wood and in vineyard and yet in this small remainder of arable ground there be gather as I see upon their account in the year of our lord 1582. 200. and 5000. hannack of wheat fertility beside infinite store of rye and barley one of our english quarter make four and a half of their hannack the soil be delicate temperate and will produce all the most excellent thing the earth bear if the spaniard will seek and labour they the vineyard vineyard of account be in buena Vista in dante in Oratana in tigueste and in the Ramble which place yield the most excellent wine of all other there be two sort of wine wine in this island Vidonia and Muluesia Vidonia be draw out of a long grape and yield a dull wine the Maluesia out of a great round grape and this be the only wine which pass all the sea of the world over and both the pole without sour or decay whereas all other wine turn to vinegar or freeze into ice as they approach the southern or northern Pole there be no where to be find fair or better melon pomegranate pomecitron fig fruit orange lemon almond and date honey and consequent wax and silk though not in great quantity yet excellent good and if they will plant there store of mulberry tree the ground will in goodness and for quantity equal if not exceed either Florence or Naples in that commodity the north side of this island abound aswell with wood as with water there grow the cedar cypress and bay tree the wild olive mastic and sauine Tree goodly procerous palm and pine-tree which shoot up into a beautiful straight talnese in the passage betwixt Oratana and Garachiro you ride through a whole forest of they the strong savour of which perfume all the air thereabouts of these there be such abundance all the island over that all their wine vessel and wooden utensil be make of they there be of these pine-tree two sort the strait pine and the other grow after the manner of our spread oak in England which will the inhabitant call the immortal tree immortal tree for that it rot neither above nor below the ground nor in the water it be near as red as Brasill and as hard but nothing so unctuous as the other kind of Pine of these they have such great one that the spaniard do faithful report that the wood of one pinetree alone cover the church of Remedios in the city of laguna which be 80. foot in length and 48. foot in breadth and that one other pinetree cover the church of s. benito in the same city which be 100 foot in length and 35. in breadth the noble and strange tree of all the island be the tree call Draco his body rise into a exceed height and greatness Draco tree the bark be like the scale of a dragon and from thence I suppose it have his name on the very top of the tree do all his arm cling and interfold together by two and by two like the mandragora they they be fashion even like the arm of a man round and smooth and as out of their finger end grow the leaf about two foot in length in fashion like to our green wild water segg this tree have not wood within its bark but only a light spongiou pith and they common make bee-hive of the body of they towards the full of the moon it sweat forth a clean vermilion gummme which they call sangre de Draco more excellent and astringe by far then that which we have from goa and from other part of the east indies by reason the jew be the only druggist of those part and to make money they falsify and multiply it with other trash four pound weight for one the first that be know to inhabit this island be call guanche but how they come thither it be hard to know because they be and be people mere barbarous and void of letter ancient inhabitant the language of the old guanche which remain to this day among they in this island in their town of Candelaria allude much to that of the moor in Barbary when Betanchor the first christian discoverer of these part come thither he find they to be no other than mere gentile ignorant of God notwithstanding I do not find that they have any manner of commerce with the devil a thing not usual among the indian gentile their religion they hold there be a power which they call by diverse name as Achuhurahan Achuhucanar Achguayaxerax signify the great the high and the maintainer of all if they want rain or have too much or any thing go ill with they they bring their sheep and their goat into a certain place and sever the young one from the dam and with this bleat on both side they think the wrath of the supreme power be appease and that he will provide they of what they want they have some notion of the immortality and punishment of soul for they think there be a hell and that it be in the pike of teyda and they call hell Echeyde and the devil Guayotta in civil affair they be somewhat regular as in acknowledge a king and confess vassalage in contract matrimony reject of bastard succession of king make of law and subject themselves to they when any child be bear they call unto they a certain woman baptism and she do with certain word pour water upon the child head and ever after this woman be assume into the number of that kindred and with she it be not lawful ever after for any of that race to marry or use copulation the exercise which the young man use be leap or run shoot the dart cast of the stone and dance in which to this hour they do both exceed glory and delight and so full of natural virtue and honest simplicity be these barbarian that it be a inviolable law among they that if their soldier do in any place public or private offer any licentious or injurious behaviour to a woman he be assure put to death the people of this country be of a goodly stature well form and of a good complexion there be among they giant giant of a incredible greatness the skull of one of they be remain in which there be eighty tooth and his body which be find bury in the sepulchre of the king of guymur of which race he be measure fifteen foot the people that dwell on the southside of the island be of the colour of a olive but those that dwell on the north-side be fair especial their woman have bright and smooth hair their common apparel apparel be a certain garment make of lamb skin like a short coat without pleat or colour or sleeve fasten together with strap of the same leather the ordinary garment for man and woman of the common sort be call Tomarco only the woman for modesty sake have another cover under their Tomarco which be a side coat down to the knee make of skin which reach down to the ground for they hold it a unseemly thing in a woman to have her breast or her foot uncover in this garment they live and in this they die and in this they be common bury for their diet diet they sow barley and bean wheat be utter unknown to they they toast their barley by the fire then do grind it in certain hand mill such as be now in Spain the flower so make they call Giffio wet it with water milk or butter it serve instead of bread also and be their great and most general sustenance they eat the flesh of sheep of goat and pork but not common for they have certain assembly like our festival Wake-day in England at which time the king in person with his own hand do give to every twenty of they three goat and a proportion of their Giffio after which feast every company come before the king show their agility in leap run wrestle dart dance and other sport they have a certain kind of honey out of a fruit call Mozan of the greatness and bigness of a pease before they be ripe they be very green when they begin to ripe they be red and when they be ripe be black nothing unlike our blackberry mozan their physic save in their taste which be exceed pleasant they eat no more but the juice of they which they call Yoya and the honey which they make of they they call they gather these mozan very ripe and do put they into the sun for a week than they break they in piece and put they into water to be boil until they come to a syrup and this be their physic for the flux and the grieving in the back and for both these disease they do also let blood in the arm head and forehead with a flintstone at their time of sow the king have appoint to every man his portion of ground that be to be sow seed how swoon they dig up the earth with goat horn and with certain word throw their seed into the ground all other work appertain unto and be perform by their woman the king do make his habitation in natural cave or hollow rock of which there be infinite store remain to this day when there be any feast make in any kingdom their feast feast have the privilege that man may with immunity pass to and fro through the enemy country yea and many time the enemy will feast one with another in their marriage marriage the man use to ask the consent of the widow or maid parent if there be any which be grant they be marry with little or no ceremony that I can learn and the marriage be not so soon make but it may be as quick break for if the husband or wife be dispose to be separate they may be so and both of they marry again with other at their pleasure notwithstanding all the child of the separate beget afterward be esteem as bastard the king only for succession sake exempt from this custom and to who for that respect it be lawful to marry with his own sister for many year this island be subject to one only king who they call adexe who be grow old his son which be nine in number conspire against he part the island into nine several kingdom all their war be to steal cattle one from another and especial the spot goat which among they be in great and religious estimation the government there be very little difference betwixt the body colour and smoothness of our english fallow deer and their goat the ancient guanche of this island have a appoint officer or embalmer answerable to the sex man or woman who wash the dead corpse do put into its body certain confection make of goat butter melt the powder of furze and of a kind of ruff stone the rind of pine-tree and other herb and do stuff the body with this every day for 15. day together put the body against the sun now on the one side now on the other funeral until it be stiff and dry all this space their friend bewail their death at the end of 15. day they wrap their body in goat skin so cunning sow together that it be marvelous and so they carry the body to a deep cave where none may have access there be of these body remain yet which have be bury these 1000 year the near port town to the city call cidade de laguna be Santa cruz sancta Cruz. from thence you ascend up the steep mountain to the city which you shall find to be most miraculous seat in the midst of a flat of ten mile in compass as if nature have prepare that place for man to build a city upon and be wall about with hill of wonderful height on all side save to the northwest from whence there be a level tract of land even to the seaside which be seven league distant there do continual arise from the sea a vapour which be circulate among so many and intricate mountain grow to be a wind and take his passage through those channel of mountain to the city to its great refresh refresh wind and in this great plain like envy for want of opposition die and let the wind blow full southeast at sea yet shall you always have the wind full northwest at the city like a true friend when you must need he from twelve a clock in the day until night the extreme dew which fall do sufficient cool the night their building be all of a open rough stone nothing fair they be very plain in their building two or three story high and no more and common but one story high in the remote part of the city it be not wall they have no chimney no not so much as in their kitchen they make only a flat hearth against a wall and there they toast their meat rather than roast it the decency of their street in commendable for when you be in the centre of the city your eye reach almost to the extreme part thereof they have no want of water the city have its name from a great stand lake at the west end of it upon which Zeni gather out of their letter by Francisco Marcolina they be relate by m. hakluyt in his 3. vol. pa. 121. in the year a thousand three hundred and fourscore Mr Nicolo Zeno be wealthy and of a haughty spirit desire to see the fashion of the world build and furnish a ship at his own charge and pass the strait of Gibraltar hold on his course northwards with intent to see England and Flanders but a violent tempest assail he at sea he be carry he know not whither till at last his ship be carry away upon the i will of Friesland where the man and most part of the good be save in vain seem that delivery that deliver up present to another executioner the islander like Neptune hungry groom or his base and black guard set upon the man who the sea have spare but here also they find a second estape by mean of a prince name zichmui prince of that and many island thereabouts who be near hand with his army come at the outcry and chase away the people take they into protection this zichmui have the year before give the overthrow to the king of Norway and be a great adventurer in feat of arm he speak to they in latin and place they in his navy wherewith he win diverse island Nicolo behave himself so well both in save the fleet by his sea-skill and in conquest of the island by his valour that Zichmui make he knight and captain of his navy s. Thomas monastery in Groenland after diverse notable exploit Nicolo arm three bark with which he arrive in Engroneland where he find a monastery of friar of the preacher order and a church dedicate to st Thomas hard by a hill that cast out fire like veswin and Aetna there be a fountain of hot water with which they heat the church of the monastery and the friar chamber it come also into the kitchen so boil hot that they use no other fire to dress their meat and put their bread into brass pot without any water it do bake as it be in a hot oven they have also small garden which be cover over in the winter time and be water with this water be defend from the violence of the frost and cold and bring forth flower in their due season the common people astonish with these strange effect conceive high of those friar and bring they present of flesh and other thing they with this water in the extremity of the cold heat their chamber which also as the other building of the monastery arc frame of those burn stone which the mouth of the hill cast forth they cast water on some of they whereby they be dissolve and become excellent white lime and so tough that be contrive in building it last for ever the rest after the fire be out serve in stead of stone to make wall and vault and will not dissolve or break except with some iron tool their winter last nine month and yet there be a fair haven where this water fall into the sea not freeze by mean whereof there be great resort of wild fowl and fish which they take in infinite multitude the fisher boat be make like to a weaver shuttle of the skin of fish fashion with the bone of the same fish and be sow together with many double they be so strong that in foul weather they will shut themselves within the same not fear the force either of sea or wind neither can the hard-hearted rock break these yield vessel they have also as it be a sleeve in the bottom thereof by which with a subtle device they convey the water forth that soak into they the most of these friar speak the latin tongue a little after this Nicolo return and die in Friesland whither his brother Antonio have before resort to he and now succeed both in his good and honour who Zichmui employ in the expedition for Estotiland Estotiland which happen upon this occasion six and twenty year before four fisherboat be apprehend at sea by a mighty and tedious storm wherewith after many day they be bring to Estotiland above a thousand mile west from Friesland upon which one of the boat be cast away and six man that be in it be take and bring to a populous city where one that speak latin and have be cast by chance upon that island in the name of the king ask they what countryman they be and understand their case he acquaint the king there with they dwell jaques l l jaq. cart. 2. cap. 10. cartier in one which they call Cudruaigni who say they often speak to they and tell they what weather will follow whether good or bad moreover when he be angry with they he cast dust into their eye they believe that when they die they go into the star and thence by little and little descend down into the horizon even as the star do after which they go into certain green field full of goodly fair and precious tree flower and fruit the frenchman tell they Cudruaigni be a devil and acquaint they with some mystery of the christian religion whereupon they condescend and desire baptism the french excuse and promise after to bring priest for that purpose they live in common together and of such commodity as their country yield they be well store they wed two or three wife a man which their husband be dead never marry again but for their widow livery wear a black wood all the day of their life besmear their face with coal-dust and grease mingle together as thick as the back of a knife they have a filthy and detestable use in marry their maiden first put they be once of lawful age to marry in a common place as harlot free for every man that will have to do with they until such time as they find a match I have see house as full of such prostitute as the school in France be full of child they there use much misrule riot and wantonness they dig their ground with certain piece of wood as big as half a sword where they sow their maize the man also do much use tobacco the woman labour more than the man in fish and husbandry they be more hardy than the beast and will come to our ship stark naked go upon snow and ice in which season they take great store of beast stag bear martern hare and fox who flesh they eat raw have first dry it in the sun or smoke and so they do their fish they have also otter weasil beavers badger coney fowl and fish great variety and one fish call Adhothuis who body and head be like to a greyhound white as snow their great jewel be chain of Esurgnie which be shellfish exceed white which they take on this manner when a captive or other man be condemn to death they kill he and then cut slash in his most fleshy part and hurl he into the river Cornibots whence after twelve hour they draw he find in those cut these Esurgnie whereof they make bead and chain they be excellent for staunch of blood thus within the gulf of canada be eighteen league he observe a feast make by Anadabijon the great Sagamo in his cabin in which eight or ten kettle of meat be set on several fire six pace asunder the man sit on both side of the room each have a dish make of the bark of a tree one appoint to divide to every man his portion before the meat be boil one take his dog and dance about the kettle from one to another and when he come before the Sagamo cast down his dog and then succeed another in the like exercise after their feast they dance with the head of their b b the Irocois with who these Estechemin algoumequin and montainer have war enemy in their hand some sing their canoas be of the bark of birch strengthen within with little circle of wood eight or nine pace long fit for active and passive carriage their cabin be low like tent cover with the say bark the roof open a foot space uncover to let in light with many fire in the midst ten household sometime together the lie upon skin one by another and their dog with they after a certain feast the algoumequin one of these three nation in league go out apart and cause all their woman and maid to sit in rank themselves stand behind sing sudden all the woman and maid cast of their mantle of skin and strip themselves naked not ashamed of their shame keep on still their Matachia which be c c bead pater-noster and chain interlace make of the hair of the porkespicke die of diverse colour their song end they cry with one voice ho ho ho and then cover themselves with their mantle which lay at their foot and after a while renew their former song and nakedness their Sagamo sit before the virgin and woman between two staff whereon be hang those enemy head and he exhort the mountainer and estechemain to the like signification of joy which then cry all together ho ho ho. when he be return to his place the great Sagamo and all his company cast off their mantle their privity only remain cover with a little skin and take each what they think good as Matachias hatchet sword kettles flesh etc. which they present to the algoulmequin after this two of each nation contend in run and the best runner be reward with present they be well set of tawny or olive colour by reason of their paint they be liar their custom give to revenge without law when a maid be fourteen or fifteen year old she have many lover and use carnal filthiness with who she please so continue five or six year and then take who she like for her husband live with he chaste all her life after except for barrenness he forsake she the husband be jealous and give present to her parent when one die they make a pit and therein put all his good with the corpse cover the same with earth and set over it many piece of wood with one stake paint red and set up on end they believe the immortality of the soul and that the dead go into far country to make merry with their friend d d m. Champlein Champlein discourse with certain savage yet live of who he learn touch their religion that they believe in one God who have create all thing that after God have make all thing he take a number of arrow and do stick they into the ground from whence man and woman spring up which have multiply ever since touch the trinity be ask a sagamo or governor answer e e the answer of a sagamo in case of religion there be one only God one son one mother and the sun which be four notwithstanding f f this somewhat agree with the manichean and Pythagorean error that God be over and above all the son be good and the sun also but the mother be naught and do eat they and that the father be not very good be ask if they or their ancestor have hear that God be come into the world he say that he have not see he but that ancient there be five man who travel towards the set of the sun meet with God who demand of they whither go you they answer we go to seek for our live God say you shall find it here but they not regard pass further and then God with a stone touch two of they who be turn into stone and he say again to the three other whither go you they answer and he reply as at first they yet pass further he take two staff and touch therewith the two foremost and transform they into staff ask the three man whither he go he say to seek his live whereupon he bid he tarry and he do so and God give he meat and he do eat and after he have make good cheer he return among the other savage and tell they all his tale this sagamo also tell that at another time there be a man which have store of tobacco and God come and ask he for his pipe which the man give he and he drink much of it and then break the pipe the man be offend hereat because he have no more pipe but God give he one and bid he carry it to his sagamo with warning to keep it well and then he shall want nothing nor any of he since the say sagamo lose the pipe and find famine and other distress this seem to be the cause why they say God be not very good be demand what ceremony they use in pray to their god he say that they use no ceremony but every one do pray in his heart as he will they have among they some savage who they call Pilotova who speak visible to the devil and he tell they what they must do as well for war as for other thing and if he shall command they to put any enterprise in execution or to kill a man with Spaniard lust by our late virgin-mother be just call Virginia whether shall I here begin with eulogy or elegy whether shall I warble sweet carol in praise of thy lovely face thou fair of virgin which from our other Britain world have win thou wooer and suitor not such as Leander who love the poet have blaze for swim over the strait betwixt Sestos and abydus to his lovely hero but which for thy sake have forsake their mother-earth encounter the most tempestuous force of the air and so often plough up Neptune plain furrow the angry ocean and that to make thou of a rude virgin not a wanton minion but a honest and christian wife or shall I change my accent and plain i for I know not of who to who to complain of those disadventure which these thy lovely lover have sustain in seek thy love what envy I know not whether of nature willing to reserve this nymph for the treasury of her own love testify by the many and continual present of a temperate climate fruitful soil fresh and fair number and great plenty of poultry chap. 5 of the religion and rite of the virginian @. i. of the virginian rite relate by master hariot now for the manner and rite of the people thus have master hariot report they believe that there be many god which they call Mantoac but of different sort and degree one only chief and great God which have be from all eternity who as they affirm when he purpose to make the world make first other god of a principal order to be as mean and instrument to be use in the creation and government to follow and after the sun moon and star as petty god and the custom manner and superstition they war a a laudonniere always one country upon another and kill all the man they can take the woman and child they bring up they cut off the hair of the head together with the skin and dry it to reserve the same as a monument of their valour after their return from the war if they be victorious they make a solemn feast which last three day with dance and song to the honour of the sun for the sun and moon be their deity their priest be magician also and physician with they they have many hermaphrodite which be put to great drudgery and make to bear all their carriage in necessity they will eat coal and put sand in their pottage three month in the year they forsake their house and live in the wood against this time they have make their provision of victual dry the same in the smoke they meet in consultation every morning in a great common house whither the king resort and his senator which after salutation sit down in a round they consult with the jawas or priest and after this they drink cassine which be very hot make of the leaf of a certain tree which none may taste that have not before make his valour evident in the war it set they in a sweat and take away hunger and thirst four and twenty hour after when a king die they bury he very solemn and upon his grave they set the cup wherein he be wont to drink and round about the grave they stick many arrow weep and fast three day together without cease all the king which be his friend make the like mourn and in token of their love cut off half their hair which they otherwise wear long knit up behind both man and woman during the space of six moon so they reckon their month there be certain woman appoint which bewail his death cry with a loud voice thrice a day at morning noon and evening all the good of this king be put into his house which afterward they set on fire the like be do with the good of the priest who be bury in their house and then both house and good burn the woman b b or cathay the man in these part cloth and shoe themselves with leather they have no bread of any kind of grain their chief food be flesh which they often eat raw either for custom or for lack of wood they eat the fat as they take it out of the ox and drink the blood hot which of our bull be count poison and the flesh they warm for they seethe it not at a fire of Ox-dung they rather may be say to negro this be their ordinary unction they have another when they go to sacrifice or incense on the top of mountain or in dark cave where there idol be use also certain ceremony to take away fear and add courage this unction be make with diverse venomous beast as spider scorpion salamander and viper which the boy in the college take and gather together wherein they be so expert as they be always furnish when the priest call for they they take all these together and burn they upon the hearth of the temple which be before the altar until they be consume to ash then do they put they in mortar with much tobacco or Petum which make they lose their force mingle likewise with these ash scorpion spider and palmer alive after this they put to it a certain seed be ground which they call Olololuchqui whereof the indian make drink to see vision for that the virtue of this herb be to deprive man of sense they do likewise grind with these ash black and hairy worm who hair only be venomous all which they mingle together with black or the fume of rosine put it in small pot which they set before their god say it be his meat and therefore call it a divine meat by mean of this ointment they become witch and do see and speak with the devil the priest be slubber with this ointment lose all fear put on a spirit of cruelty by reason whereof they do very bold kill man in their Hak. have this calendar set down their month name in order the indian describe they by peculiar picture common take of the principal feast therein they account their week by thirteen day they have also a week of year which be likewise thirteen they reckon by a certain wheel which contain four week that be two and fifty year in the midst of this wheel be paint the sun from which go four beam of line in a cross of distinct colour Greene blue red and yellow and so the line betwixt these on which they note by some picture the accident that befall any year as the spaniard come mark by a man clad in Red the last night when this wheel be run about they break all their vessel and stuff put out their fire and all the light say that the world shall end at the finish of one of these wheel and it may be at that time and then what shall such thing need upon this conceit they pass the night in great fear but when they see the day begin to break they present beat many drum with much other mirth and music say that God do prolong the time with another age of two and fifty year and then begin another wheel the first day whereof they take new fire for which they go to the priest who fetch it out of a mountain and make a solemn sacrifice and thanksgiving the twenty day of each month be call by several name the first Cipactli which signify a spade and so the rest a house a dog a snake a eagle a temple and the like by this calendar they keep thing in memory above nine hundred year since the indian of Culhua do believe that the god have make the world they know not how and that since the creation four sun be pass and that the five and last be the sun which now give light unto the World the first sun forsooth perish by water and all live creature therewith opinion of five sun the second fall from heaven and with the fall slay all live creature and then be many giant in the country the three sun be consume by fire and the four by tempest of air and wind and then mankind perish not but be turn into ape yet when that four sun perish all be turn into darkness and so continue five and twenty year and at the fifteen year God do form one man and woman who bring forth child and at the end of other ten year appear this five sun new bear which after their reckon be now in this year 1612. nine hundred and eighteen year since three day after this sun appear they hold that all the heaven and down to the centre when they speak thereof many of their wife for they may have many follow the sepulcher of their husband they allow not marriage with the sister of which they have a Curiania they receive the spaniard with great joy and for pin needle bell glass and such trifle give they many string of pearl for four pin they will give a peacock for two a pheasant for one a turtle dove and when they ask what they shall do with this new merchandise of pin and needle see they be naked they show they the use to pick their tooth and to pick out thorn in their foot these indian have ring of gold and jewel make with pearl after the form of bird fish and beast they have also the touchstone for their metal and weight to weight the same thing not elsewhere find in India they make their tooth white with a herb which all the day they chew in their mouth chap 2 of cumana and paria @. i. of the people and strange creature in cumana CVmana be a province name of a river call cumana b b gom cap. 76. where certain franciscan 1516. build they a monastery and the spaniard be very diligent in the fish for pearl about c c P.M. dec. 7. lib. 4. that time three dominican go fourscore mile west from thence to preach the gospel and be eat of the indian which hinder not but other of the same order found they a monastery in Ciribici near Maracapana both these order take pain with the indian to convert they and teach their child to write and read and to answer at mass and the spaniard be so respect that they may safe walk alone through all the country but after two year and a half the indian whether for their too much employment in the Pearl-fishing or for other cause rebel and kill a hundred spaniard slay the friar one of which be then say mass and as many indian as they find with they which the spaniard of Domingo soon after revenge the loss of d d gom. c. 78. in commodity that accrew by those pearl which have amount to diverse million of gold they fetch their wood from Margarita a island four mile to the north and their water from cumana which be two and there be fish or sea-monster which from the middle upward resemble man with beard hair and arm the e e cap. 79. people of cumana go naked cover only their shame at feast and dance they pain themselves or else anoint themselves with a certain gum in which they stick feather of many colour they cut their hair above the ear and will not suffer it to grow on any place of their body esteem a beard man a beast they take great pain to make their tooth black and account they woman which have they white they black they with the powder of the leaf of a certain tree call gay these leave they chew after they be fifteen year old they mix that powder with another of a kind of wood and with chalk of white shell burn in manner as the eastern indian use their betele and Arecca with chalk of oyster and this mixture they bear continual in their mouth still chew it that their tooth be as black as coal and so continue to their death they keep it in basket and box and sell it in the market to some which come far for it for gold slave Cotton and other merchandise this keep they from pain and rot of the tooth the maid go naked only they bind certain band hard about their knee to make their hip and thigh seem thick which they esteem no small beauty the marry woman live honest or else their husband will divorce they the chief man have as many wife as they will and if any stranger come to lodge in one of their house they make the fair his bed-fellow their marriage these also shut up their daughter two year before they marry they all which time they go not forth nor cut their hair after which there be make a great feast and very many bid which bring their variety of cheer and also wood to make the new spouse a house a man cut off the bridegroom hair before and a woman the bride and then they eat and drink with much excess till night this be the lawful wife and the other which they marry afterward obey this. they give their spouse to be deflower to their Piaces so they call their priest which these reverend father account their pre-eminence and prerogative the husband their honour the wife their warrant the man and woman wear collar bracelet pendant and some crown of gold and pearl the man wear ring in their nose and the woman brooch on their breast whereby by at first sight the sex be discern the woman shoot run leap swim as well as the man their pain of travel be small they till the land and look to the house while the man hunt and fish they be high-minded treacherous and thirsty of revenge their chief weapon be poison arrow which they prepare with the blood of snake and other mixture all of both sex from their infancy learn to shoot their meat be whatsoever have life as horseleech bat grasshopper spider bee louse worm raw sodden fry and yet their country be replenish with good fruit fish and flesh this diet or as some say their water cause spot in their eye which dim their sight they have as strange a fence or hedge for their garden and possession namely a thread of Cotton or Bexuco as they call it as high as a man girdle and it be account a great sin to go over or under the same and he which break it they certain believe shall present die so much safe be their thread weave with this imagination than all our stonewall the e e P.M. dec. 8. lib. 7. cumanois be much addict to hunt wherein they be very expert their strange creature and kill lion and drink their dance and drunkenness in which they will spend eight day together especial at the marriage or coronation of their king many gallant will then meet together diverse dress some with crown and feather some with shell about their leg in stead of bell to make a noise some otherwise all paint with twenty colour and figure he that go worst seem best take one another by the hand they dance in a ring some backward some forward with a world of variety grin sing cry counterfeit the deaf lame blind fish weave tell of story and this continue six hour and then they eat and drink before he which dance most now he which drink most be the most complete and accomplish gallant and now beyond counterfeit drunkenness set they together in brave swagger quarrel other play the swine spew up the former to make way for other liquor and they add hereunto the fume of a herb which have the like drunken effect it seem to be tobacco this perhaps will not seem strange to some see these savage custom of drink dance smoke swagger so common with we in these day it may indeed seem strange to our forefather if their more civil more sacred ghost may return and take view of their degenerate moon which be take for man and wife and for the great god they have great fear of the sun when it thunder or lighten say that he be angry with they they fast when there be any eclipse especial the woman for the marry woman pluck their hair and scratch their face with their nail the maid thrust sharp fishbone into their arm and draw blood when the moon be at full they think it be wound by the sun for some indignation he have conceive against she when any comet appear they make a great noise with drum and hallow think so to scare it away or to consume it believe that those comet portend some evil among their many idol and figure which they honour as god they have one like a saint Andrews cross which they think preserve they from night-spirit and they hang it on their newborn child they call their priest their priest Piaces who maiden-head-rite we before mention they be their physician and magician they cure with root and herb raw sod and pound with the fat of bird fish and beast with wood and other thing unknown to the people with abstruse and dark word which themselves understand not they suck and lick the place where the pain be to draw out the evil humour and if the when one call @. 3 of Trinidado and paria in the year 1497. some add a year more g g p. martyr dec. 1. lib. 6. gom part. 2. cap. 84. Christopher Columbus seek new discovery after the suffering of unsufferable heat and calm at sea whereby the hoop of his vessel break and the freshwater not able further to endure the hot indignation of that now-believed burning-zone flee out of those close prison into the lap of that father of water the ocean for refuge he come at last to Trinidado the first land he encounter he call by that name either for devotion now that his other hope be dry up with the heat or wash into the sea by the violent shower above-board and the less but not less dangerous which flow from his cask within or else for the three mountain which he there descry once this discovery of land so ravish his spirit by the inexpected delivery from danger as easy carry his impotent thought into a double error the one in place earthly paradise in this island to which opinion for the excellency of the tobacco there find he shall happy have the smoky subscription of many humorist to who that fume become a fool paradise which with their brain and all pass away in smoke the other be that the earth be not round like a ball but like a pear the upper swell whereof he esteem these part hence Columbus sail to paria and find out the pearl-fishing pearl fish of which Petrus Alphonsus a little after make great commodity by trade with the savage he be assail with eighteen canoas of cannibal h h p. martyr Dec. 1. l b. 8 of the cannibal see chapter 13. one of which he take with one cannibal and a bound captive who with tear show they that they have eat six of his fellow and the next day he must have go to pot too to he they give power over his jailor who with his own club kill he still lay on when his brain and gut come forth and testify that he need not further fear he in Haraia or paria they find plenty of salt which the foreman in nature shop and her chief workman the sun turn and kern from water into salt his workhouse for this business be a large plain by the watersside here the sepulcher of their king and great man seem not less remarkable they lay the body on a kind of hurdle or grediron of wood under which they kindle a gentle fire whereby keep the skin whole they by little and little consume the flesh these dry carcase they hold in great reverence and honour for their household god in the year i i gem. cap. 85. 1499. Vincent pinzon discover cape saint Augustine and sail along the coast from thence to paria but why stand we here peddle on the coast for pearl salt and tobacco let we rouse up high spirit and follow our english guide for Guiana only let i first have leave to mention concern the superstition of these part northward from Guiana what it please sir Walter Raleigh to impart unto i from the relation of a very understanding man of that country who he use for a interpreter these people worship the sun Relat. S.W.R. who they imagine as the fabulous grecian tell of his chariot and horse wherewith young Phacton sometime set the world on fire to be draw into a chariot by tiger which be the most fiery and fierce beast among they in honour therefore of the sun and for sustenance of his chariot-beast they careful wash the carcase of their dead and lay they forth in the night for repast unto the tiger weary with their long and late journey in the day for so they believe that after sunset these beast be to this end dismiss from their labour and that vicissitude wherein David observe the wisdom of divine providence that when it be night the wild beast go forth to seek their prey psal. 104.20 ^^ 22 23. which when the sun arise and call man forth of their house to labour return to their den be blind by they apply to this their superstition they likewise have a tradition among they that their ancestor in time past neglect thus to prepare the corpse of such as die for the tiger diet or not wash they so neat as behove the tiger make hereof a complaint to the sun as not able to do his work if not allow their wont cate whereupon the sun send one among they brandish a terrible fiery sword and so dreadful assault the place of their habitation and the soil cover with long grass that all fall on fire and a hundred thousand of the inhabitant be destroy a terrible warning hereafter to be more diligent in these tiger-devotion which according they perform to this day chap 3 of Guiana and the neighbour nation on the coast and within the land @. i. discovery of Guiana by sir WALTER Raleigh in the year 1595. a a sir Walter Raleigh treatise of Guiana sir Walter Raleigh have before receive intelligence of this rich and mighty empire set forth for the discovery and on the two and twenty of march anchor at point Curiapan in Trinidado and search that island which he find plentiful he take the city of saint joseph and therein Antony Berreo the spanish governor leave his ship he go with a hundred man in boat and a little galley and with some indian pilot pass along that admirable confluence of river as by the corpse du Guardiano unto Orenoque as great a commander of Rivers as the emperor of Guiana of soldier and although we have before mention somewhat thereof yet this his peculiar place require some further consideration this river Orenoque or Baraquan since of this discovery call Raleana run from quito in Peru on the west it have nine branch which fall out on the north side of his own main mouth on the south side seven thus many arm have this giantlike stream to be his purveyor which be always fill his never-filled mouth seem by this their natural officiousness incorporate thereunto and to be but wide gape of the same spacious jaw with many island and break ground as it be so many morsel and crumb in his greedy chap still open for more though he can even in winter when his throat be glibbe altogether swallow these yea these force he for fear of choke to the string make of the herb tocon little yet able to endure the strength of a horse their arrow a ell long which they will shoot twice as fast as our man they have leather shield their elder man lead the rank if they may be so call which have none to marshal or order they and with great shout and show the enemy the bone of their slay friend they enter into a fierce battle their captive they convey in the midst of their army home to their territory unto who the man will not stick to give their sister or daughter to perform all the duty of a wife and feed they with the best till they redemand the same out of their flesh the man be employ if it be long before the slaughter in hunt fowl fish the woman in garden or gather oyster when that dismal day approach knowledge be give and the man woman in site they have their summer from October to April the rest their winter the like be note in the east indies at the hill of Balegate where that ridge part winter and summer in the same nearness to learned man be of opinion that all which the indian make mention of be not above four hundred year which may be impute to their want of writing in stead of writing they use their Quippos Quippos these Quippos be memorial or register make of cord in which there be diverse knot and colour signify diverse thing these be their book of history of law ceremony and account of their affair there be officer appoint to keep they call Quipocamayos which be bind to give account of thing as notary and register they have according to the diversity of business sundry cord and branch in every of which be so many knot little and great and string tie to they some red some green and in such variety that even as we derive a infinite number of word from the letter of the alphabet so do they from these kind and colour and at this day they will keep account exact with they I do see say acosta a handful of these string wherein a indian woman do carry as it be write a general confession of all her life and thereby confess herself as well as I can have do in write paper with string for the circumstance of the sin they have also certain wheel of small stone by mean whereof they learn all they desire by heart thus you shall see they learn the paternoster creed and the rest and for this purpose they have many of these wheel in their churchyard they have another kind of Quippos with grain of maize with which they will cast hard account which may trouble a good arithmetician with his pen in the division they be no less witty q q id. ibid. c. 26. if not more in thing whereto they apply themselves than the man of these part they teach their young child all art necessary to the life of man every one learn what be needful for his person and family and not appropriate himself to one profession as with we one be a tailor another a weaver or of other trade every man be his own weaver carpenter husbandman and the like but in other art more for ornament then necessity they have goldsmith painter potter and weaver of curious work for nobleman and so of the rest no man may change the fashion use in his own country when he go into another that all may be know of what country they be for their marriage of wool otherwise of reed and this do he lead she thence with he if she commit adultery she be punish with death when the husband die she carry a mourn weed of black a year after and may not marry in i. of their calendar and holiday before we speak of the perwian festival time it be not amiss to take some more general view of their calendar they a a accost l 6. c. 3. divide their year into so many day just as we do and into so many month or moon to make the computation of their year certain they use this industry upon the mountain about cusco there be twelve pillar set in order and in such distance as every month one of these pillar do note the rise and set of the sun they call they Saccanga by mean whereof they teach and show the feast and the season fit to sow and reap and for other thing they do certain sacrifice to these pillar of the sun every month have his peculiar name and feast they sometime begin the year in january but since a Ingua call Pachacuto which signify a reformer of the temple begin their year in December by reason as it seem of the sun return from Capricorn their near tropic I read not of any week they observe for which they have not so certain a rule as the sun course be for the year and the moon for the month they observe in Peru two kind of feast some ordinary which fall out in certain month of the year and other extraordinary which be for certain cause of importance every month of the year they make feast and sacrifice and have this alike the offering of a 100 sheep but of unlike colour and form according to the month in the first in seventeen year travel and experience in Russia and other country adjoin have before see france and the low country by sir EDWARD HORSEYS mean and in the company and charge of master William Mericke agent for the company I arrive in Muscovia a. 1573. and have some smack in the greek by affinity thereof in short space attain the ready knowledge of their vulgar speech the sclavonian tongue large extent of the sclavonian tongue the most copious and elegant language of the world with some small difference of dialect come near the polish Lettois and Transylvanian and all those country adjacent be use by merchant in Turkey also Persia and in India I read their chronicle write and keep in secret by a great prince of that country Knez Misthislofskie russian chronicle who out of his love and favour impart unto i many secret observe in the memory of his fourscore year time of the nature and government of that State vasy or Basilius great Duke of Russia to omit thing of former age vasy Andreowich have enlarge his dominion upon the pole and Swethen and special on the crimme tartar leave his people strong and rich his country divide into four part and two son the elder of five year call volica Knez juan Vasilliwich which reign after he the other of two year duke of vaga juan grow up comely in person endue with excellent gift his two son juan and Andrew juan succeed at twelve year age he marry Nastacia Romanova which become so wise and virtuous that she be much love and fear a long time carry the whole sway her husband be young and riotous she rule with admirable wisdom so that he cast off the yoke of homage to the crym conquer diverse tartarian prince the empire of Casan and Astracan 2700. mile down the Volga from Moscow and by a general council of his prince prelate entitle emperor and noble be crown and style the emperor and great duke of Volladamiria Muscovia Cazan and Astracan etc. his conquest grow with his year he take from the king of Poland the famous city of Pollozca the great city of Smolensca Doragabus Vasma and many other town with much riches and infinite number of captive seven hundred mile within their confine Lituania and bela Russia goodly town of traffic and country yield wax flax hemp tallow hides corn and cattle in abundance he grow puissant and proud overmighty for his next neighbour and bloody in all his conquest when his good queen Nastacia die Nastacia the Empress make a saint second wife a Tartar she be canonize a saint and to this day worship in their church by she he have two son juan and Theodore the emperor after this marry one of the chirca by who he have no issue that he will be know of the manner of this marriage be strange and heathenish which I forbear out of their own history to relate by this marriage he be much strengthen by the tartar better soldier than the native of who he make use to curb his prince and noble which be discontent with his cruel rob and incessant murder of his nobility he set forward with 100000. horse and 50000. foot with provision of cannon and munition towards livonia and Swethia kill man woman and child in his way to Novogrod and Plesco the two great town of traffic in all the east with the narve which three stand triangle wise at the end of the Baltic sea within the sound in this last he build a castle call juan Gorod and cause the eye of the architect to be bore out thence he enter the confine of livonia Narue castle Architect blind that he may not do the like to other send Knez juan Grinscoy to besiege Newhous which be take with all the town in the way to dorp this also yield and the tartar carry away eight thousand captive the merchandise and treasure be send to Nogrod for the emperor use he proceed divide his army into four part ten thousand be appoint to draw the ordnance over the freeze lake take all in his way thirty wall town and castle near the eastern sea within two hundred mile compass drown cruelty burn ravish maid and wife strip they naked notwithstanding the cold tie they by two and three at their horse tail and drag they some alive some dead the way and street lie full of carcase of every age and sex these livonians be account the fair people in the World infinite number be send into Russia with infinite treasure six hundred church be rob and destroy he and his tartar at last come to revel besiege and batter it with twenty cannon the inhabitant by night make up the breach by carry and cast hot and cold water which freeze so thick ice-fortification that after six week siege and 20000. cannon shoot spend with loss of 7000. he haste away the sudden thaw also make he to leave much of his artillery behind with former booty baggage and 30000. man in his retire enrage with fury for this repulse and loss he come back to the narve spoil the town of all the riches and merchandise kill man woman and child and give the spoil to his tartar which breed no small emulation in his ruff captain thence he march to plescove alias Vobsco where he intend to do the like easy believe those which report that these two town and Novogrod have practise against he that by their mean he have sustain his loss at revel Plesco by a magician deliver but there meet he a magician Mikula sweat which that town hold their oracle who with bold imprecation and exorcism call he bloodsucker and devourer of christian flesh swear by his angel that he shall not escape death by a present thunderbolt if he or any of his do touch the least child hair in that city which God by his angel do preserve for better purpose than his rapine that therefore he shall get he thence before the fiery cloud of God wrath be raise which he may behold hang over his head it be a very great and dark storm at that instant the emperor tremble at these word desire prayer for his deliverance and forgiveness of his cruel thought I see this impostor a foul creature he go naked winter and summer endure extreme frost and heat his holiness can not endure i he do many strange thing by magical illusion and be much follow and fear there of prince and people novogrod spoil with horrible cruelty the emperor return to Novogrod where all his captive and prisoner english trade in those part by master WILLIAM METHOLD the gulf of Bengala famous for its dimension extend itself from the cape call comorijne lie in 8. degree of north latitude unto Chatigan the bottom thereof which be in 22. degree be not less as the coast lie then a 1000 english mile and in breadth 900. limit on the other side by cape Singapura which lie in 1. degree of south latitude wash the coast of these great and fertile kingdom viz. Ziloan Bisnagar Golchonda Bengala Arreccan Pegu and Tanassery and receive into its * * sinus Gangeticus bosom many navigable river which lose their note and name in the eminent neighbourhood of the famous Ganges who unknown head pleasant stream and long extent have among those heathen inhabitant by the tradition of their forefather gain a belief of cleanse all such sin as the body of those that wash therein bring with they for which cause many be the pilgrim that resort from far to this last jubilee with some of who I have have conference and from their own report I insert this their belief the island of Zeloan our nation have only look upon passant the portugal that claim all east India by donation hold a great part of this in subjection Zeloan or Zeilan and with such assurance that they believe they can make it good against all their enemy yet be not they the only lord thereof for the natural inhabitant have also their king common call the king of Candy with who the dane have not long since a fruitless treaty for commerce which fall short of their expectation they fortify upon the main Candy not far from Negapatnam at a place call Trangabay with what success or hope of benefit I can relate the first kingdom upon the main be that ancient one of Bisnagar rend at this time into several province or government hold by the p p captain governor naicke of that country in their own right for since the last king who decease about fifteen year since there have arise several competitor for the crown unto who the naicke have adhere according to their faction or affection from whence have follow a continual civil war in some part of the country and such extreme want and famine in most of it that parent have bring thousand of their young child to the sea side sell there a child for five d d two shilling six penny sterling s. Thome see before in Balbie etc. fanum worth of rice transport from thence into other part of India and sell again to good advantage if the gain be good that arise from the sale of soul in this kingdom lie the town of saint Thome inhabit and govern by portugal who notwithstanding must acknowledge some dependency from the Naicke that hold that part of the country of who after some siege endure by author of this laborious volume be embolden to publish such remarkable thing as have fall within the compass of my observation it be a small town but populous unwall ill build and worse situate within all the spring be brackish and without overflow with every high sea for almost half a mile about it be first a poor fisher town from whence it take the name it yet retain afterward the conveniency of the road make it a fit residence for merchant and so continue with increase of trade since our and the dutch nation frequent this coast the climate be very healthful climate and season hight and kill wind and the year divide in their account into three different season whereof march April May and june they call the hot season and not without good cause for the sun be return into their hemisphere do not alone scorch the earth with his pierce beam but even the wind which shall assuage his fury add great fire and yearly about mid may with a strong westerly gale bring off the land a sensible heat as when a house be on fire such as be near to leeward can hardly endure and this so penetrate that the door and window be shut the house be notwithstanding so warm that the chair and stool admit hardly the use they be make for without cool they and the place where we abide by often sprinkle of water but the extremity hereof neither last long nor come often only five or seven day in a year and then but from nine or ten a clock in the forenoon until four or five in the afternoon at which time a cool breeze from off the sea qualify again this intolerable heat wherein many of the native be in their travel suffocate and perish and of christian a Dutchman as he be carry in his palamkeene Peter jacobson r. household-god they have all of they their Penates or household god which the chief of the family as the elder brother keep always at his house for which they once a year make a feast marriage but the kindred be assemble eat it up in marriage it be the child duty to attend upon the parent care who find in their own tribe and as near as they can in their own kindred no degree of consanguinity hinder but brother and sister a fit wife for their son he though of full age submit his consent without see she account it unreasonable to recompense his parent care and trouble in his education with give earring bracelet and other jewel according to her quality unto the bride two or three wear clothes unto the mother with some present to the father and then bear the whole charge of the wedding from which large expense it sometime happen that want keep many a long time unmarried until their endeavour in the world have supply they with mean to defray the charge but this not hinder the rich sort they common marry their child very young the husband five year of age the wife not above three year and many such couple have I see put together wherein the parent conceive they have do a act of year of age and the woman 10. or 11. they meet again and become so well acquaint that many be mother at 12. year of age and some I have hear no virgin at nine to proceed of what year soever they be elder brother if he himself be not elder for seldom do brethren divide themselves but all of they though many live together in own family bring their gain whatsoever it be unto the common stock cherish with a admire duty their old indigent parent and live together in most commendable unity widow if the husband die the wife may not marry again and which be most unreasonable not the young one though never know of man who happen to be widow in their infancy must not only continue so but be make the drudge to the whole family not permit to wear their jewel good or clean clothes or upon Thoaba thoaba 20. rule Spain one year juseph succeed at this time the Ommian race be dispossess of the chalifate and that of abbas succeed abderramen of the Ommian family possess himself of Spain after which it be separate from the asian chalifate and become a kingdom and these ommians call themselves emirelmumenim this be an. h. 142. in the year 149. he begin the mezquit at Corduba the chief of all other in his dominion an. 171. he die and be bury at Corduba he leave eleven son and nine daughter isen the elder succeed and war on his brother Zulema who he put to flight he take Toledo Zulema sell all his challenge in Spain and pass the sea to Barbary as do Abdalla also another brother isen an. 177. send abdelmelic with a great army into France which spoil and subdue Narbone with so great a part of the country that isen perfect with the fifth of those spoil the temple of Corduba which his father have begin the christian also of Narbone carry earth thither from their own country he build the bridge at Corduba he be munificent and just he prosper in France war with alfonsus king of Gallicia and have reign seven year seven month and seven day die leave his kingdom to his son Alhacam a. 179. he be wise and fortunate have seven thousand slave for his guard three thousand renegado and two thousand eunuch he personal judge poor man cause and be liberal in alm he overcome in battle Zulema and Abdalla his uncle ship of dane as our story call they or norman or other infest Spain slay one and subject the other he die an. 206. leave nineteen son and one and twenty daughter abderramen his son succeed he recover the town which in late schism the christian have get an. 229. fifty ship and fifty four galley arrive at Lisbon the next year a great number of ship come and besiege Seville and often fight with the Arab and spoil their dominion with fire and sword carry away every thing of value and kill very many abderraman have a great battle with they but neither part prevail an. 236. Corduba be pave and water bring thither in pipe of lead abderraman die an. 238. leave five and forty son and two and forty daughter Mahomet his son succeed who much prevail against the christian slay many and an. 245. take Toledo by composition sixty norman ship that year burn gelzirat Alhadia and the mezquit and thence proceed into Africa and there commit many spoil after which they return and winter in Spain and in the spring wen home an. 273.
